A huge cryosleep facility being built for Project Ark (the species preservation plan) of the <EOT Special Council>. Located beneath Kenya, Africa, it is run by Magus, an autonomous supercomputer built by Dr. Sophia Nate. Thousands were to sleep there to survive the coming Aerogator invasion, but construction stopped when the DC War broke out. A similar facility, the Moon Cradle, exists on the Moon.

A class of anti-alien mobile weapons evolved from fighters. Their <Tesla Drive>, a reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, lets them fly unaided and outmaneuver fighters, making them the bane of <Personal Troopers>, which can't fly.

An island off the Marquesas in the South Pacific where Meteor 3 fell in S.C. 179. The <EOTI Institute> was based there to study it, and its <EOT> and anti-alien weapon research became the <DC>'s military foundation. Fortified for <EOT> secrecy, the island's defenses center on air defense and air power, owing to its geography.

Children born with a gift for piloting and fighting in humanoid mobile weapons. With superb dynamic vision, reflexes and data processing, they adapt easily to such machines, and are said to be a byproduct of advanced combat simulator games. Needing no long training or drugs, they are sought as pilots by many groups.

A common measure of <Telekinesis Alpha Pulse> readings. Those with strong concentration tend to score high, and past a certain level they have superhuman telekinesis. It also shows a subject's <T-LINK System> compatibility.

Short for Extra Over Technology: the alien super-technology found in Meteor 3, the meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island. Analyzed by the <EOTI Institute> under Dr. Bian Zoldark, it brought revolutionary advances in many fields, especially military technology. However, the <EOT Special Council> controlled it, so it was rarely applied to society at large.

Extra Over Technology Inquiry Organization. Formed in S.C. 180 to analyze and study the <EOT> found in Meteor 3, the mysterious meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island. Top scientists were gathered from around the world, with Bian Zoldark, hailed as a peerless genius, serving as director.

A federal body handling Meteor 3 and Aerogator secrets, made up of 13 core Federal Security Committee members; it oversees the <EOTI Institute>. Its chair is committee vice chairman Carl Stresemann. Aware of the Aerogators' might from Meteor 3 and <EOT> findings, they saw Bian's call for all-out resistance as dangerous and monitored and obstructed him.

A long-established leader in shipbuilding, power plants, aircraft and more, with a strong aerospace record and a key defense industry role. It makes the F-28 Messer fighter, the F-32 Schwert and Peregrine-class battleships.
Abbreviation of <Armored Module>.

A project of the <Earth Sphere Defense Plan> at the Earth Federation Army's Langley Base in North America, developing humanoid assault weapons. Counterpart to the Far East branch's <SRX Project>, it uses no <EOT> at all, at chief developer Dr. Marion Radom's wish. Meant to yield the next mainstay unit, it is shifting toward custom units for aces.

A project of the <Earth Sphere Defense Plan> at the Earth Federation Army's Izu Base, developing special humanoid weapons for anti-alien combat. Led by Ingram Plissken, it builds prototypes called the "R Series" that make heavy use of <EOT>. Some carry the <T-LINK System>, but Ingram's team struggled to find compatible pilots (who also need a certain flair for piloting and fighting in humanoid machines). One solution was a gamble: scouting the public through "Burning PT," a robot fighting game modeled on a Personal Trooper's controls.

A barrier (attack-nullifying defense) that directly projects non-material energy, such as EM waves, gravity waves, telekinesis or photons. Types are chosen by attack kind and work by neutralizing, diffusing, compressing, distorting and more. The surface may form a thin crystal film from air elements, so a field can seem to "shatter" as it fades.
Short for Mass Amplitude Preemptive-strike Weapon, a large-scale, wide-area preemptive weapon. By area, MAPWs divide into linear, radial and scatter types. Also called "map weapons."

Humanity's first sealed space colony, completed in S.C. 075. It houses the United Colony Government and the <United Colony Corps> headquarters. Colony history up to the 180s was one of hardship: a 076 civil war over failed space-adaptation surgery on the first emigrants; a 157 terror attack for autonomy (the Nozomi Incident); a 172 bulkhead bombing (the Hope Incident); and a 184 BC-weapon terror attack (the Elpis Incident), each with many deaths. But from the early 160s, a movement (NID4) sought autonomy from the Earth Federation government by peaceful means. Its leader, Bryan Midcrid, won over Earth's public opinion, achieved colony independence in 184, and became the United Colony Government's first president (at the same time, the Federation Space Force stationed in the colonies became the <United Colony Corps>, with Maier as commander-in-chief). There are ten colonies, all in the L4 area: No. 1 Elpis, No. 2 Nozomi, No. 3 Hoffnung, No. 4 Wish, No. 5 Espoir, No. 6 Hope, No. 7 Space, No. 8 Esperanza, No. 9 Speranza and No. 10 Nadezhda.
See <Tactical Instructor Corps>.

A man-machine interface being developed by Eagret Feff, a scientist at the giant cryogenic facility <Earth Cradle>, with Adler's backing. It links pilot and machine directly for smoother control. The machine can also act on the pilot, forcibly raising their resolve and reaction speed. At present, pilots cannot endure long use of it without some form of enhancement.

Formed in SE 184, when ten space colonies united into an independent nation, by reorganizing the Federation Space Force units stationed there. Nominally separate, it is in practice under Federation Army control, which some of its officers resent. Its demanding space missions have drawn top talent.

A former Federation Army school for humanoid weapon pilots, founded around the same time as the <Tactical Instructor Corps>. It first retrained existing pilots on <Personal Trooper> and other humanoid weapons, but its aims changed entirely once Adler Koch took charge. He wanted pilots trained from the start for humanoid weapons. He secretly gathered children with no family ties and superb reflexes and visual acuity, and brought in Dr. Aguila Setome of the Japan Special Brain Medical Institute to erase and alter their memories. Adler then used mind control, drugs and special training to create, quickly, humans specialized for humanoid weapon combat: the Boosted Children. They were sorted into classes named after metals, such as Aurum (gold), Argent (silver), Bronzo (bronze), Hierro (iron) and Latune (brass), each adjusted for different roles. Perhaps due to the harsh methods, very few achieved outstanding results. The inhumane methods and poor results led to the School's dissolution, but the Boosted Children's training continued at the <DC>.

Proposed in SE 182 by Major General Norman Slay of the Joint Chiefs and still ongoing. As named, it aims to defend the Earth Sphere from the Aerogators. Its hubs, Langley (N. America), Izu (Far East) and Aviano (S. Europe), develop anti-Aerogator weapons. Many Federation leaders doubt it.

The Earth Federation Government's global military, built on the old UN Special Forces. Economy and government still rely on inter-state coordination, but the military is unified worldwide. Branches keep traits of the old national armies they grew from.

A global government that grew from a provisional UN body amid the turmoil after the 2012 meteor disaster (Double Impact). Though it oversees the former nations, now autonomous states, it never unified all human politics, and those states inherited the small and mid-scale conflicts that predated it.
Generic name for a high-end handheld.
Abbreviation of <Divine Crusaders>.

Tactical Cybernetics Operating System (a tactical motion-thinking OS). The OS of <Personal Trooper> and other humanoid weapons. For example, if the pilot chooses to punch an enemy, the AI calculates both units' positions and picks the most efficient, suitable pattern from the stored motion data. This frees pilots from complex controls: they focus on assessing the situation and make minimal inputs, while the machine automatically picks fitting motions and executes their intent. Pilots can also choose motion pattern types and priorities, optimizing movement for their preferences and habits.

A telekinesis sensor and amplifier developed by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi of the <SRX Project>. It extracts the T-Alpha Pulse, a deep brainwave governing thought, to move objects and assist in piloting. It can also create a force field, the TK Field, for barriers or to strike enemies. Amplified thought extends the user's sixth sense, akin to touch, over a wide area, aiding enemy detection and tracking. However, it depends on the user's mental state, and excessive linking strains the brain heavily. In Ingram and Kenzo's projects, people with T-Alpha Pulses above a set level are called telekinetics.

A military society Dr. Bian Zoldark founded from the <EOTI Institute>, foreseeing an alien invasion. It aims to set up a strong military regime in the Earth Sphere to resist alien conquest. Its core forces are secretly built <Armored Module> units and aircraft like the F-32. Federation officials and some officers have joined, and the <United Colony Corps> backs it. But anti-Federationists, liberation fighters and terrorists also join for their own ends, so it is far from united.

A high-efficiency reaction drive developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute>. By altering gravitational mass (weight) and inertial mass (resistance to motion) separately, it accelerates propellant to propel objects efficiently, a form of gravity control. It eases atmospheric flight and space travel, but early units were so big only ships could mount them. Analysis of Meteor 3's <EOT> greatly advanced gravity physics, making the drive far stronger and smaller. Starting with the <DC>'s Armored Modules, it can now fit 20-meter humanoid weapons.

An overtechnology research institute in Colorado, North America, founded by Bian Zoldark in SE 171. It has produced geniuses like robotics authority Jonathan Kazahara and Eric Wong. Though most members left for the <EOTI Institute>, it still pursues its own <EOT> research, <Tesla Drive> upgrades and the Grungust series. Named after inventor Nikola Tesla and scientist Wilhelm Reich.
A deep brainwave tied to thought, identified by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi. Used to judge telekinetic aptitude.

A unit formed to research and develop combat techniques for humanoid mobile weapons and to create their motion data. The basic motion data in the <TC-OS> installed on today's Personal Troopers is what they produced through repeated test operations. It consisted of six elite members: its captain Kar-wai Lau, Kai Kitamura, Tempest Hawker, Sänger Sombold, Elzam V. Branstein and Gilliam Jaeger. The unit disbanded after an incident in SC 184, but its colorful members and their achievements have made it half-legendary both inside and outside the Federation Army.
Special humanoid weapons, aka Super Robots: generally units over 40 m with unique power sources or systems.

A substance found in Meteor 3. It does not occur naturally, at least in the solar system, and was reportedly sealed in an apparently artificial container when found. Each piece is a rice-grain-sized metal holding vast energy. Meteor 3 held six, analyzed by the <EOTI Institute>; several reached the Federation Army through various deals (involving Major Ingram Prisken of the SRX Project). The Tronium Engine converts Tronium's near-limitless energy into power, at a rate per unit time too high to measure. Since engine materials of Earth's technology can't withstand it, a limiter is fitted. Energy output also climbs exponentially as power rises, making output control very difficult.

The general term for humanoid weapons built to counter the 10m+ jointed mobile weapons the Aerogators are believed to have. The first Personal Trooper was the PTX-001 Gespenst by <Mao Industries>, rolled out in SE 180. Features include easy weapon replacement via manipulators and high mobility over terrain through bipedal walking and hovering. Thanks to the <TC-OS>, pilots just assess the situation and make minimal inputs while the machine picks fitting motions to carry out their intent. Costs and the Earth Federation Army leadership's lack of threat awareness have slowed production, so tanks and fighters remain its mainstay.
Abbreviation of <Personal Trooper>.

A heavy machinery maker founded in SE 176 by Ting Mao, Yuan Mei Long and others in Selevis City on the Moon. Originally making bipedal lunar work machines, it now mainly builds Personal Troopers. Its president is Ting's daughter Ling Mao.

A meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island, off the Marquesas in the South Pacific, in New Century 179. The <EOTI Institute> believes the Aerogators sent it to Earth on purpose: it appeared suddenly in the L5 area before falling, slowed itself before impact, and held <EOT> sealed inside as if meant to be read by others. The name follows Meteors 1 and 2, which hit New York and Moscow in the old era and badly set back Earth's civilization.
A uniform force field around the unit bends kinetic energy crossing its spherical edge and disperses it along the boundary. Even EM waves lose their form, so beams and solid rounds may be nullified.

A giant cryosleep facility being built for the <EOT Special Council>'s Project Ark (species preservation plan). Built under Kenya, Africa, it is run by Magus, an autonomous supercomputer made by Dr. Sophia Nate. Thousands were to sleep there to survive the coming Aerogator invasion, but work halted when the <DC War> broke out. After the war, DC remnants seized it as their base. A similar facility, the Moon Cradle, exists on the Moon.

Anti-alien mobile weapons evolved from fighter jets. The <Tesla Drive>, a thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, lets them fly alone and outmaneuver fighters. The DC's main force in the DC War, they are still made by <Isurugi Heavy Industries> as Federation mainstays.

Anti Sensor and Radar Suffia-field: a spherical anti-detection field or its generator. Read "Asres." An ECM used by DC remnants, it forms a spherical field of any radius around the emitter. Radar waves hitting it bend around the sphere and keep going, so the receiver gets no echo at all. It only lasts briefly, but DC remnants have often ambushed the Federation Army with ASRS units.

Children born with a gift for piloting and fighting in humanoid mobile weapons. With superb dynamic vision, reflexes and data processing, they adapt easily to such machines, and are said to be a byproduct of advanced combat simulator games. Needing no long training or drugs, they are sought as pilots by many groups.

A common measure of <Telekinesis Alpha Pulse> readings. Those with strong concentration tend to score high, and past a certain level they have superhuman telekinesis. It also shows a subject's <T-LINK System> compatibility.

Short for Extra Over Technology: the alien super-technology found in Meteor 3, the meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island. Analyzed by the <EOTI Institute> under Dr. Bian Zoldark, it brought revolutionary advances in many fields, especially military technology. However, the <EOT Special Council> controlled it, so it was rarely applied to society at large.

Extra Over Technology Inquiry Organization. Formed in New Century 180 to analyze and study the <EOT> found in Meteor 3, the mysterious meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island. Top scientists worldwide gathered under director Bian Zoldark, hailed as the genius of his age. It became the parent of the <DC>, and its scientists went on to develop many weapons and systems for the <DC>.

A high Federation body on Meteor 3 and Aerogator secrets, formed by 13 core Federation Security Council members. It oversaw the <EOTI Institute>. Its chair was Carl Stresemann, the Security Council's vice-chair. Aware of the Aerogators' might from Meteor 3 and <EOT> research, they saw Bian's call for all-out resistance as dangerous and spied on and obstructed him, which helped drive Bian to raise the <DC>. All members, Carl Stresemann included, died in the L5 Campaign, ending the council.

A Federation Army reform and buildup plan Bryan Midcrid proposed after the <L5 Campaign> against alien threats to humanity. It drives battleship construction and new mainstay unit production. Its final stage is a vast <EOT>-based gravity shield network, the "Aegis Shield."

A long-established leader in shipbuilding, power plants and aircraft, strong in aerospace and key to the arms industry. While supplying Federation fighters like the F-32 Schwert, it had ties to the <EOTI Institute> and secretly mass-produced the Lion series in the <DC War>. Ironically, the series became the Federation's mainstay after the <L5 Campaign>, and its aid to the DC was pardoned to secure production.

A force based on Nebiim, an automated planet that suddenly appeared at L5, which attacked the Earth Sphere with insect-like mobile weapons such as the Megillot ("Aerogators" is Earth's code name). They sought to use humanity's combat prowess for themselves, but lost in Operation SRW, the L5 Campaign's final battle. After the war, they proved to be humans mentally conditioned by someone, a fact kept top secret.
Abbreviation of <Armored Module>.

An assault humanoid mobile weapon project. The <SRX Project>'s equal counterpart, it mostly avoids <EOT> at chief developer Dr. Marion Radom's wish. Meant to make the next Federation mainstay, it is shifting to custom units for aces.
Anti-alien special humanoid weapon project. It builds units like the R Series that actively apply <EOT>.

A barrier (attack-nullifying defense) that directly projects non-material energy, such as EM waves, gravity waves, telekinesis or photons. Types are chosen by attack kind and work by neutralizing, diffusing, compressing, distorting and more. The surface may form a thin crystal film from air elements, so a field can seem to "shatter" as it fades.
Short for Mass Amplitude Preemptive-strike Weapon, a large-scale, wide-area preemptive weapon. By area, MAPWs divide into linear, radial and scatter types. Also called "map weapons."

The Aerogator conflict that followed the <DC> War in New Century 187. The Aerogators, based on Nebiim (code name: White Star), an automated planet that suddenly appeared at L5, raided the Earth Sphere with insect-like weapons such as the Megillot. They sought to use humanity's combat prowess for themselves, but lost in Operation SRW, the L5 Campaign's final battle. After the war, they proved to be humans mentally conditioned by someone, a fact kept top secret.

Humanity's first sealed space colony, completed in S.C. 075. It houses the United Colony Government and the <United Colony Corps> headquarters. Colony history up to the 180s was one of hardship: a 076 civil war over failed space-adaptation surgery on the first emigrants; a 157 terror attack for autonomy (the Nozomi Incident); a 172 bulkhead bombing (the Hope Incident); and a 184 BC-weapon terror attack (the Elpis Incident), each with many deaths. But from the early 160s, a movement (NID4) sought autonomy from the Earth Federation government by peaceful means. Its leader, Bryan Midcrid, won over Earth's public opinion, achieved colony independence in 184, and became the United Colony Government's first president (at the same time, the Federation Space Force stationed in the colonies became the <United Colony Corps>, with Maier as commander-in-chief). There are ten colonies, all in the L4 area: No. 1 Elpis, No. 2 Nozomi, No. 3 Hoffnung, No. 4 Wish, No. 5 Espoir, No. 6 Hope, No. 7 Space, No. 8 Esperanza, No. 9 Speranza and No. 10 Nadezhda.
See <Tactical Instructor Corps>.

A man-machine interface being developed by Eagret Feff, a scientist at the giant cryogenic facility <Earth Cradle>, with Adler's backing. It links pilot and machine directly for smoother control. The machine can also act on the pilot, forcibly raising their resolve and reaction speed. At present, pilots cannot endure long use of it without some form of enhancement.

Formed in New Century 184, when 10 space colonies united as an independent nation, by reorganizing the Earth Federation Space Force stationed there. Nominally separate, it is in practice under Federation Army control, to some officers' displeasure. Its demanding space missions draw top talent. In late New Century 186, it declared war on the Federation alongside the DC and, holding most forces in space, quickly seized space superiority. It then supported the DC on the ground, but surrendered to the Federation Army after commander-in-chief Maier V. Branstein was killed. Yet this was to prepare for the coming alien war; indeed, many of its units joined Operation SRW, the L5 Campaign's final operation. After the war it fell under Federation control and its leaders were replaced, leaving the name hollow, but it still holds most space forces.

A former Federation Army school for humanoid weapon pilots, founded around the same time as the <Tactical Instructor Corps>. It first retrained existing pilots on <Personal Trooper> and other humanoid weapons, but its aims changed entirely once Adler Koch took charge. He wanted pilots trained from the start for humanoid weapons. He secretly gathered children with no family ties and superb reflexes and visual acuity, and brought in Dr. Aguila Setome of the Japan Special Brain Medical Institute to erase and alter their memories. Adler then used mind control, drugs and special training to create, quickly, humans specialized for humanoid weapon combat: the Boosted Children. They were sorted into classes named after metals, such as Aurum (gold), Argent (silver), Bronzo (bronze), Hierro (iron) and Latune (brass), each adjusted for different roles. Perhaps due to the harsh methods, very few achieved outstanding results. The inhumane methods and poor results led to the School's dissolution, but the Boosted Children's training continued at the <DC>.

Proposed in New Century 182 by Major General Norman Slay of the Federation Joint Staff. As named, it aimed to defend the Earth Sphere from the Aerogators, arming against them at Langley (N. America), Izu (Far East) and Aviano (S. Europe) bases. It became the basis of the <Aegis Plan>.

The Earth Federation Government's global military, built on the old UN Special Forces. Economy and government still rely on inter-state coordination, but the military is unified worldwide. Branches keep traits of the old national armies they grew from.

A global government that grew from a provisional UN body amid the turmoil after the 2012 meteor disaster (Double Impact). Though it oversees the former nations, now autonomous states, it never unified all human politics, and those states inherited the small and mid-scale conflicts that predated it.
Generic name for a high-end handheld.
Abbreviation of <Divine Crusaders>.

Tactical Cybernetics Operating System (a tactical motion-thinking OS). The OS of <Personal Trooper> and other humanoid weapons. For example, if the pilot chooses to punch an enemy, the AI calculates both units' positions and picks the most efficient, suitable pattern from the stored motion data. This frees pilots from complex controls: they focus on assessing the situation and make minimal inputs, while the machine automatically picks fitting motions and executes their intent. Pilots can also choose motion pattern types and priorities, optimizing movement for their preferences and habits.

The <DC>'s uprising from late New Century 186 into 187. Rebelling against the Earth Federation Government and Army, it took bases across the Earth Sphere in an <Armored Module> blitz. But leader Bian Zoldark died in the Hagane's raid on Aidoneus Island, and the DC fell into chaos and lost.

A telekinesis sensing and amplifying device developed by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi of the <SRX Project>. It extracts the T-Alpha Pulse, a special deep brainwave of thought, to move objects and assist in piloting mobile weapons. It can also create a force field, the TK Field, as a barrier or to ram enemies. Amplified thought also widens the user's special perception (a touch-like sixth sense), allowing some tracking of enemies. But it depends on the user's mental state, and excessive linking severely strains the brain. Kenzo's project calls people with T-Alpha Pulses above a set level "telekinetics."

A military group Dr. Bian Zoldark formed from the <EOTI Institute>, foreseeing an alien invasion. Its goal was a strong military regime over the Earth Sphere to resist alien invaders. Besides EOTI members, it drew Federation officials, some soldiers, anti-Federationists and liberation fighters, and the <United Colony Corps> cooperated. In late New Century 186, it rose against the <Earth Federation Government> and Army, seizing bases across the Earth Sphere in an <Armored Module> blitz. But the path Bian and United Colony Corps commander Maier V. Branstein chose cut both ways. By becoming the "enemy," they aimed to give humanity a taste of its plight and spur it to face an unheard-of threat, but a long civil war risked draining Earth's own strength. So they sought a quick end to the DC War while sparing part of the enemy (Federation) forces. Bian also meant to entrust the Earth Sphere's future to anyone strong enough to defeat him. This contradiction arguably led to his defeat and emboldened those who used the DC for selfish ends. Bian died in the Hagane's raid on DC headquarters, and the DC fell into chaos and lost.

A high-efficiency reaction drive developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute>. By altering gravitational mass (weight) and inertial mass (resistance to motion) separately, it accelerates propellant to propel objects efficiently, a form of gravity control. It eases atmospheric flight and space travel, but early units were so big only ships could mount them. Analysis of Meteor 3's <EOT> greatly advanced gravity physics, making the drive far stronger and smaller. Starting with the <DC>'s Armored Modules, it can now fit 20-meter humanoid weapons.

An overtechnology research institute in Colorado, North America, founded by Bian Zoldark in New Century 171. It produced geniuses like robotics expert Jonathan Kazahara and Eric Wong. Most staff moved to the <EOTI Institute>, but it still pursues <EOT> research, <Tesla Drive> upgrades and the Grungust series. It is named after inventor Nikola Tesla and scientist Wilhelm Reich. Its current director is Jonathan Kazahara.
A deep brainwave tied to thought, identified by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi. Used to judge telekinetic aptitude.

A unit formed to research and develop combat techniques for humanoid mobile weapons and to create their motion data. The basic motion data in the <TC-OS> installed on today's Personal Troopers is what they produced through repeated test operations. It consisted of six elite members: its captain Kar-wai Lau, Kai Kitamura, Tempest Hawker, Sänger Sombold, Elzam V. Branstein and Gilliam Jaeger. The unit disbanded after an incident in SC 184, but its colorful members and their achievements have made it half-legendary both inside and outside the Federation Army. After the <L5 Campaign>, it was re-formed with Kai Kitamura as its captain.
Special humanoid weapons, aka Super Robots: generally units over 40 m with unique power sources or systems.

A substance found in Meteor 3. It does not occur naturally, at least in the solar system, and was reportedly sealed in an apparently artificial container when found. Each piece is a rice-grain-sized metal holding vast energy. Meteor 3 held six, analyzed by the <EOTI Institute>; several reached the Federation Army through various deals (involving Major Ingram Prisken of the SRX Project). The Tronium Engine converts Tronium's near-limitless energy into power, at a rate per unit time too high to measure. Since engine materials of Earth's technology can't withstand it, a limiter is fitted. Energy output also climbs exponentially as power rises, making output control very difficult.

Humanoid mobile weapons built to counter the 10m-plus jointed mobile weapons the Aerogators are thought to possess. The first Personal Trooper was the PTX-001 Gespenst by <Mao Industries>, rolled out in SC 180. Manipulators make replacing weapons easy, and bipedal walking and hovering give high mobility over terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot just reads the situation; with minimal input, the unit automatically picks fitting motions to do what the pilot intends.
Abbreviation of <Personal Trooper>.

A <DC> project for interstellar travel using mid-sized ships. Led by Major Filio Presty, it develops interstellar ships and trains their pilots. After the DC fell, it continued under the Federation, backed by <Isurugi Heavy Industries>; its units and systems are also used militarily. "TD" stands for both "<Tesla Drive>" and "Terrestrial Dream."

A heavy machinery maker founded in SE 176 by Ting Mao, Yuan Mei Long and others in Selevis City on the Moon. Originally making bipedal lunar work machines, it now mainly builds Personal Troopers. Its president is Ting's daughter Ling Mao.

A meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island, off the Marquesas in the South Pacific, in New Century 179. The <EOTI Institute> believes the Aerogators sent it to Earth on purpose: it appeared suddenly in the L5 area before falling, slowed itself before impact, and held <EOT> sealed inside as if meant to be read by others. The name follows Meteors 1 and 2, which hit New York and Moscow in the old era and badly set back Earth's civilization.

ReEOTH PLAN. ReEOTH (Reios) stands for "Reliable Extra Over Technological Hybrid": a highly reliable alien-tech composite. The plan fundamentally reworks unstable <EOT> by introducing Earth's latest technology to raise its reliability and stability. It aims not only to upgrade existing EOT units but to apply ReEOTH to R-series successors and future mass-produced units.
A uniform force field around the unit bends kinetic energy crossing its spherical edge and disperses it along the boundary. Even EM waves lose their form, so beams and solid rounds may be nullified.

A giant cryogenic hibernation facility built under Project Ark (a plan to preserve the species) promoted by the <EOT Special Council>. Located underground in the Kenya region of Africa, it is managed by Meigas, an autonomous supercomputer developed by Dr. Sophia Nate. Several thousand people were to enter hibernation there to survive the coming war of invasion by the Aerogators, but construction was halted when the <DC War> broke out. After the war, DC remnants seized it and made it their base, but it was heavily damaged in battle with the Kurogane's unit. It was then placed under the jurisdiction of a special Federation Army research institute. A similar facility, the "Moon Cradle," also exists on the Moon.

Anti-alien mobile weapons evolved from fighter jets. The <Tesla Drive>, a thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, lets them fly alone and outmaneuver fighters. The DC's main force in the DC War, they are still made by <Isurugi Heavy Industries> as Federation mainstays.

An island off the Marquesas in the South Pacific where the mysterious Meteor 3 fell in SC 179. The <EOTI Institute> studied it there, and its <EOT> and anti-alien tech became the <DC>'s base of power. Fortified for EOT secrecy, the island's defenses centered on air power. Most facilities were destroyed fighting the Septuagint in the <L5 Campaign>, ending its use as a fortress. The Federation now controls it and has sealed off nearby waters.

A group of grotesque beings that appeared in the Earth Sphere from SC 187 to 188. Their main force was a series of mysterious bioweapons called the Einst series, which at first repeatedly engaged in baffling local battles. The only ones with clear will, intelligence and the ability to communicate were the high-ranking Einst called Regisseur and a girl named Alfimi; their organization resembled that of bees or ants. The Einst seem to have existed in another dimension (Einst Space) since ancient times, watching the actions of intelligent life in our world, but details are unknown. Their goal was to annihilate humanity, which fights endlessly and disturbs the tranquility of the universe, and create new intelligent life; in the end, they sought to link Einst Space with our world and invade it. The Einst clashed with the Hagane, Kurogane and Hiryu Custom many times. In the final battle, Neu Regisseur fused with the White Star and became the gigantic mobile weapon Stern Neu Regisseur, but was defeated by the Kurogane and Hiryu Custom. After Stern Neu Regisseur's destruction, the Einst series units active around the world met the same fate.

The Inspectors are a group of aliens who came from another star system to audit Earth's civilization. Judging that humanity, with its insatiable fighting spirit, would eventually disturb the order of the galaxy, they sought to bring the Earth Sphere under their control. The name "Inspectors" was one their combat commander Vigagi used for convenience during a battle with the Hiryu Custom, and it became Earth's code name for them. Their true name is therefore unknown. They began their armed invasion in SC 187, and with a lightning campaign seized the <White Star>, the Moon and key parts of North America. However, caught up in the Earth Federation Army's counteroffensive "Operation Plantagenet" and the chaos caused by the mass appearance of the <Einst> series, they were forced to withdraw from Earth. Later, they were defeated in the decisive battle with the Kurogane and Hiryu Custom at the White Star, where Supreme Commander Wendolo and other key members were killed, and the Inspectors were wiped out. Some theorize, though, that they were merely an advance force.

The conflict waged by the Inspectors in SC 187-188. The Inspectors were alien auditors of Earth's civilization from another star system. Deciding humanity's endless will to fight would one day upset galactic order, they sought to rule the Earth Sphere. Invading in SC 187, they took the Moon and North America in a blitz. Then, caught in the chaos of the Einst swarms, they had to leave Earth and were wiped out by the Kurogane and Hiryu Custom.

An industrial machinery maker headquartered in the Dalian region of China. The company is small and little known, but its technology is excellent, and before the <DC War> it was involved in projects such as building space plants. After the <Inspector Incident>, it came under the umbrella of <Isurugi Heavy Industries>, and is developing the humanoid mobile weapon <Gestalt> based on the VT series of unmanned industrial machines.

A force based on Nebiim, an automated planet that suddenly appeared at L5, which attacked the Earth Sphere with insect-like mobile weapons such as the Megillot ("Aerogators" is Earth's code name). They sought to use humanity's combat prowess for themselves, but lost in Operation SRW, the L5 Campaign's final battle. After the war, they proved to be humans mentally conditioned by someone, a fact kept top secret.
Abbreviation of <Armored Module>.

AMN stands for Armored Module Network. A network that quickly and accurately relays one <Armored Module>'s combat data to other units and shares it among them. It was once developed by the <EOTI Institute> and <DC>, but slow data exchange kept it from adoption.

An assault humanoid mobile weapon project. The <SRX Project>'s equal counterpart, it mostly avoids <EOT> at chief developer Dr. Marion Radom's wish. Meant to make the next Federation mainstay, it is shifting to custom units for aces.

Short for Global Expanded Stamp out Tactics works ALTogether (Simultaneous Enhanced Integrated Sweep Tactics System). Humanoid weapons built by <Wong Heavy Industries> after the L5 Campaign for the <Aegis Plan>'s next-gen mainstay trials. Based on VT-series industrial machines, with a special network system.

After the war it fell under Federation control and its leaders were replaced, leaving the name hollow, but it still holds most space forces.

A group from a parallel world, brought by the dimensional transfer device System XN. Formerly that world's Federation special forces, they aided the DC remnants' uprising after the <L5 Campaign>. They aimed to perfect System XN and sustain war with XN-equipped units and the artificial "W Series," but fell to the Hagane and Hiryu Custom.

Shura Gods are the weapons used by the Shura, powered by the life energy of their pilots. They come in ranks such as "Retsu-class," "Go-class" and "Cho-class." The lowest, Retsu-class Shura Gods, can be piloted by any Shura with a certain level of haki (life energy) and skill. Go-class and Cho-class Shura Gods, however, are pickier about their riders; becoming their pilot requires matching strength, trials and rituals. Once a pilot is chosen, no one else can basically board or operate the machine until that pilot dies. Some say Go-class and Cho-class Shura Gods have a will of their own and refuse anyone they have not accepted as their pilot (an unfit pilot will have their haki drained and die). Shura Gods of Go-class and above were built with lost technology, and today's Shura cannot develop new ones. Their numbers are therefore limited, and some have been in use for centuries. A few Shura Gods are also said to remain sealed, with no pilot found. Pilots of Go-class Shura Gods are respected among the Shura and hold a certain authority. Becoming a pilot of a Cho-class Shura God is a prerequisite for the rank of Shura general. Retsu-class Shura Gods were modeled on the surviving Go-class ones; their performance is far lower, but they can be mass-produced.

Though it oversees the former nations, now autonomous states, it never unified all human politics, and those states inherited the small and mid-scale conflicts that predated it.

The title of semi-organic weapons created by the ancient Chinese to fight the demons and monsters called the "Hyakuja." They have autonomous thinking circuits and can act on their own, but cannot show their true power unless a telekinetic (a strong psychic) they have accepted as their pilot is aboard. In some cases, a normal human can also board and pilot one, but at the cost of having their soul power (life force) absorbed by the Chokijin, and in the worst case they die. The only Chokijin confirmed so far are RyuKoOh and KoRyuOh (RyuOhKi and KoOhKi). However, Chokijin have ranks such as the "Four Spirits," "Four Gods" and "Four Fiends," so units other than RyuKoOh and KoRyuOh are thought to exist, though details are uncertain.
Generic name for a high-end handheld.
Abbreviation of <Divine Crusaders>.

Tactical Cybernetics Operating System (a tactical motion-thinking OS). The OS of <Personal Trooper> and other humanoid weapons. For example, if the pilot chooses to punch an enemy, the AI calculates both units' positions and picks the most efficient, suitable pattern from the stored motion data. This frees pilots from complex controls: they focus on assessing the situation and make minimal inputs, while the machine automatically picks fitting motions and executes their intent. Pilots can also choose motion pattern types and priorities, optimizing movement for their preferences and habits.

The <DC>'s uprising from late New Century 186 into 187. Rebelling against the Earth Federation Government and Army, it took bases across the Earth Sphere in an <Armored Module> blitz. But leader Bian Zoldark died in the Hagane's raid on Aidoneus Island, and the DC fell into chaos and lost.

A telekinesis sensing and amplifying device developed by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi of the <SRX Project>. It extracts the T-Alpha Pulse, a special deep brainwave of thought, to move objects and assist in piloting mobile weapons. It can also create a force field, the TK Field, as a barrier or to ram enemies. Amplified thought also widens the user's special perception (a touch-like sixth sense), allowing some tracking of enemies. But it depends on the user's mental state, and excessive linking severely strains the brain. Kenzo's project calls people with T-Alpha Pulses above a set level "telekinetics."

A military group Dr. Bian Zoldark formed from the <EOTI Institute>, foreseeing an alien invasion. Its goal was a strong military regime over the Earth Sphere to resist alien invaders. Besides EOTI members, it drew Federation officials, some soldiers, anti-Federationists and liberation fighters, and the <United Colony Corps> cooperated. In late New Century 186, it rose against the <Earth Federation Government> and Army, seizing bases across the Earth Sphere in an <Armored Module> blitz. But the path Bian and United Colony Corps commander Maier V. Branstein chose cut both ways. By becoming the "enemy," they aimed to give humanity a taste of its plight and spur it to face an unheard-of threat, but a long civil war risked draining Earth's own strength. So they sought a quick end to the DC War while sparing part of the enemy (Federation) forces. Bian also meant to entrust the Earth Sphere's future to anyone strong enough to defeat him. This contradiction arguably led to his defeat and emboldened those who used the DC for selfish ends. Bian died in the Hagane's raid on DC headquarters, and the DC fell into chaos and lost.

A high-efficiency reaction drive developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute>. By altering gravitational mass (weight) and inertial mass (resistance to motion) separately, it accelerates propellant to propel objects efficiently, a form of gravity control. It eases atmospheric flight and space travel, but early units were so big only ships could mount them. Analysis of Meteor 3's <EOT> greatly advanced gravity physics, making the drive far stronger and smaller. Starting with the <DC>'s Armored Modules, it can now fit 20-meter humanoid weapons.

An overtechnology research institute in Colorado, North America, founded by Bian Zoldark in New Century 171. It produced geniuses like robotics expert Jonathan Kazahara and Eric Wong. Most staff moved to the <EOTI Institute>, but it still pursues <EOT> research, <Tesla Drive> upgrades and the Grungust series. It is named after inventor Nikola Tesla and scientist Wilhelm Reich. Its current director is Jonathan Kazahara.
A deep brainwave tied to thought, identified by Dr. Kenzou Kobayashi. Used to judge telekinetic aptitude.

A unit formed to research and develop combat techniques for humanoid mobile weapons and to create their motion data. The basic motion data in the <TC-OS> installed on today's Personal Troopers is what they produced through repeated test operations. It consisted of six elite members: its captain Kar-wai Lau, Kai Kitamura, Tempest Hawker, Sänger Sombold, Elzam V. Branstein and Gilliam Jaeger. The unit disbanded after an incident in SC 184, but its colorful members and their achievements have made it half-legendary both inside and outside the Federation Army. After the <L5 Campaign>, it was re-formed with Kai Kitamura as its captain.
Special humanoid weapons, aka Super Robots: generally units over 40 m with unique power sources or systems.

A substance found in Meteor 3. It does not occur naturally, at least in the solar system, and was reportedly sealed in an apparently artificial container when found. Each piece is a rice-grain-sized metal holding vast energy. Meteor 3 held six, analyzed by the <EOTI Institute>; several reached the Federation Army through various deals (involving Major Ingram Prisken of the SRX Project). The Tronium Engine converts Tronium's near-limitless energy into power, at a rate per unit time too high to measure. Since engine materials of Earth's technology can't withstand it, a limiter is fitted. Energy output also climbs exponentially as power rises, making output control very difficult.

A rebellion that took place in SC 186 at the Earth Federation Army's Coatsland Base in Antarctica. At the time, the base was holding an unveiling ceremony for the Shirogane, the first ship of the cutting-edge Space Noah-class multipurpose battleships, and for the Granzon, a humanoid mobile weapon developed by the <EOTI Institute>. This was a cover, however: behind the scenes, peace talks were under way with extraterrestrial intelligent beings code-named the "Guests." The terms amounted to Earth's near-total surrender to the Guests, and many who knew the truth were outraged. During the talks, Dr. Shu Shirakawa, one of the Granzon's developers and its test pilot, suddenly attacked the Guests' starship. He then turned on the Federation Army as well, leaving Coatsland Base in ruins. The incident ended negotiations with the Guests. The <DC> rose up right afterward, and the incident triggered the wars that followed (the <DC War>, the <L5 Campaign> and the <Inspector Incident>). Before the talks, the Guests had appeared above Coatsland Base aboard an <Aerogators> starship, so at the time many considered the Guests and the Aerogators one and the same. Today, after the <Inspector Incident>, the prevailing theory is that the Guests' ship was a disguise, and that they are not Aerogators but a power closely tied to the <Inspectors>.

Formed after the <L5 Campaign> by Van Vat Tran, uniting <DC> remnants and anti-Federation forces with <Shadow Mirror>'s help. Rising up in SC 187 to unify the Earth Sphere by force, it truly opposed alien invaders and made a truce with the Federation when the Inspectors came. In the North America recapture operation, Van died in a Shadow Mirror scheme and the group collapsed. Some remnants still hide, waging guerrilla war on the Federation.

Humanoid mobile weapons built to counter the 10m-plus jointed mobile weapons the Aerogators are thought to possess. The first Personal Trooper was the PTX-001 Gespenst by <Mao Industries>, rolled out in SC 180. Manipulators make replacing weapons easy, and bipedal walking and hovering give high mobility over terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot just reads the situation; with minimal input, the unit automatically picks fitting motions to do what the pilot intends.
Abbreviation of <Personal Trooper>.

A <DC> project for interstellar travel using mid-sized ships. Led by Major Filio Presty, it develops interstellar ships and trains their pilots. After the DC fell, it continued under the Federation, backed by <Isurugi Heavy Industries>; its units and systems are also used militarily. "TD" stands for both "<Tesla Drive>" and "Terrestrial Dream."

A gigantic spherical space fortress the <Aerogators> used as their base in the <L5 Campaign>. Its official name is "Autonomous Planet Nebiim"; White Star is Earth's code name for it. Inside are mobile weapon plants, a spaceport, 1G living areas with simulated weather, multiple farms and more, making it effectively a mobile space colony. Some theorize it was meant to carry large numbers of Earthlings, with their strong fighting spirit and combat ability, back to the Aerogators' home world, but this is uncertain. Late in the L5 Campaign, it was heavily damaged and shut down by an all-out attack from Earth's Operation SRW allied space fleet, and after the war it was placed under Earth Federation Army control. In SC 187, however, it was seized by the <Inspectors>, aliens who invaded the Earth Sphere, and became their base. Later still, it fused with Neu Regisseur, leader of the <Einst>, becoming the gigantic weapon Stern Neu Regisseur. It shifted into another dimension with the Kurogane and Hiryu Custom, and was destroyed after a fierce battle with them.

A heavy machinery maker founded in SE 176 by Ting Mao, Yuan Mei Long and others in Selevis City on the Moon. Originally making bipedal lunar work machines, it now mainly builds Personal Troopers. Its president is Ting's daughter Ling Mao.

Metal cells with self-repair and self-evolution abilities, created by Dr. Egret Fehu. They can also erode matter, rapidly restructuring anything they touch, greatly enhancing the material's properties and bringing it under their control. Development began before the <DC War>, and their performance leapt forward after a sample was obtained of the autonomous, self-aware metal cells (Zfylud Crystal) used in <Aerogators> mobile weapons. During the <Inspector Incident>, Machine Cells were also used in the Thrudgelmir and Bergelmir, humanoid mobile weapons of the <Neue DC>, displaying astonishing regenerative power.

A meteorite that fell on Aidoneus Island, off the Marquesas in the South Pacific, in New Century 179. The <EOTI Institute> believes the Aerogators sent it to Earth on purpose: it appeared suddenly in the L5 area before falling, slowed itself before impact, and held <EOT> sealed inside as if meant to be read by others. The name follows Meteors 1 and 2, which hit New York and Moscow in the old era and badly set back Earth's civilization.

ReEOTH PLAN. ReEOTH (Reios) stands for "Reliable Extra Over Technological Hybrid": a highly reliable alien-tech composite. The plan fundamentally reworks unstable <EOT> by introducing Earth's latest technology to raise its reliability and stability. It aims not only to upgrade existing EOT units but to apply ReEOTH to R-series successors and future mass-produced units.
A uniform force field around the unit bends kinetic energy crossing its spherical edge and disperses it along the boundary. Even EM waves lose their form, so beams and solid rounds may be nullified.
A huge trailer carrying PTs by land: a tractor with a mobile command post plus a self-propelled container.
A Federation Army multirole fighter. 2D thrust-vectoring nozzles and large canard delta wings let it handle air combat and ground attack alike.

An upgraded <Isurugi Heavy Industries> fighter. Built for any battlefield, it excels in air combat at all altitudes and carries a heavy payload. Special-material flexible wings, a buried cockpit and long-TBO modules set it apart.

An <Isurugi Heavy Industries> multirole fighter. Built for any battlefield, it excels in air combat at all altitudes and carries a heavy payload. Special-material flexible wings, a buried cockpit and long-TBO modules set it apart.
Grungust Type 2's flight mode. Using R-series transformation tech, it transforms over twice as fast as the first Grungust.
Air defense system with SAMs, an MLRS (multiple rocket launcher system), railguns and more.

The first R-series Personal Trooper developed by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-1." A close-combat unit with high mobility and attack power. It inherits the strengths of its predecessors, the RTX-009 Huckebein 009 (plasma generator type) and PTX-006 Wildraubtier. Like the Wildraubtier, it transforms into a flight mode (R-Wing), and often leads the R Series in surprise attacks and reconnaissance in force. To deal reliable damage, it carries solid-ammo weapons for close and mid range. It also has the <T-LINK System>, enabling attacks that apply the special force field it generates, the TK Field.

The second R-series PT developed by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-2." A heavy artillery PT built around beam weapons, carrying the <Tronium> Engine that powers the SRX. Its firepower and armor are high, but engine output is unstable and mobility low. In the R Series it provides suppressive fire and fire support.

The second R-series PT developed by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-2 POWERED." A heavy artillery PT built around beam weapons, carrying the <Tronium> Engine that powers the SRX. Its firepower and armor are high, but engine output is unstable and mobility low. In the R Series it provides suppressive fire and fire support. Equipping plus parts such as the Hyzol Launcher heavy metal particle cannon and shoulder armor makes it the R-2 Powered. When combined into the SRX, the R-2's pilot adjusts Tronium Engine output, handles damage control, and runs medical checks on the R-1 and R-3 pilots. Since the R-2 has no <T-LINK System>, its pilot needn't have Telekinesis.

The third R Series Personal Trooper built by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-3." A light command and long-range PT, it excels at target acquisition and intel gathering and carries remote weapons based on the <T-LINK System>. Only telekinetics can pilot it, making it SRX Team Captain Aya Kobayashi's de facto personal unit.

The third R Series Personal Trooper built by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-3 POWERED." A light command and long-range PT, it excels at target acquisition and intel gathering and carries remote weapons based on the <T-LINK System>. Only telekinetics can pilot it, making it SRX Team Captain Aya Kobayashi's de facto personal unit. Fitted with a Plus Part carrying the T-LINK Flight System, it becomes the heavy bomber form R-3 Powered.

The first RW Series PT built by the <SRX Project>. Official name: "REAL PERSONAL TROOPER TYPE-GUN." Originally a high-output heavy metal particle cannon, it was miniaturized for a certain purpose and given a PT mode so it could move and fight alone. Its new Tronium Engine outdoes the R-2's, giving it more power and firepower than any other R Series unit, but its output is extremely unstable. Though effectively the fourth R unit, it was never named "R-4"; Mao Industries developed it in secret on the Moon under the codename "ARGAN."

A mysterious humanoid mobile weapon piloted by Ingram. Despite its name, it's no R-GUN upgrade, but a unit summoned from another dimension by unknown means. Its torso is an upside-down R-GUN design, perhaps marking Ingram's turn from ally to enemy. Details are unknown, but it far exceeds the R-GUN in size and combat power. "Rivale" is German for "rival." Earth's ID code for it is "AGX-13 Hanged Gun."
The R-1's flight mode, mainly used for travel and recon in force. Its nose is the shield the R-1 uses in PT mode.
An upgraded space fighter used by the United Colony Corps and others. Its side units have front and rear rockets of equal thrust.
A space fighter used by the United Colony Corps and others. Its side units have front and rear rockets of equal thrust.

A prototype all-purpose, one-hit-kill Personal Trooper from the <SRX Project>, made up of the R-1, R-2 Powered and R-3 Powered. Official name: "SUPER ROBOT X-TYPE." Its development concept: "A humanoid mobile weapon combining the traits of Super Robots and Personal Troopers, able to turn the tide of battle alone or as three separate units." The project defined the SRX as three normal-sized (20m class) Personal Troopers that combine into a 50m-class <Super Robot>, letting it use its power flexibly: separated against many weak foes or when working with other PTs, and combined to concentrate the R Series' power against a few strong foes. Its firepower is outstanding, but its <Tronium> Engine's output is hard to regulate, and in battle it must constantly project a TK Field with the <T-LINK System> to help hold the combination, which heavily strains the T-LINK user. For now, combinations per sortie and combat time are limited.

A captured <DC> mass-production <Armored Module> Lion with upgraded weapons and armor. It uses spare <Personal Trooper> parts from the Hückebein, Gespenst, Alteisen and more. Its arms were swapped out entirely for PT arms, and folding slashing blades were fitted to its legs, so it can handle the close combat the Lion was weak at. A stopgap conversion halfway between a PT and an AM, but with high potential.

A <Personal Trooper> developed by the <ATX Project>. Based on the PTX-003 Gespenst Type-T kept as a test unit, it was modified to extremes under the concept of "a unit that can break through head-on with overwhelming firepower." Nearly all its weapons are solid-ammo arms for close to mid range, and at the insistence of its developer, Dr. Marion Radom, it uses no high-risk <EOT> at all. Peerless in close combat, it can match a <Super Robot>'s attack power in the right pilot's hands. It was meant to join the MP Gespenst Mk-II as a (semi-)main Federation unit, to be named "Gespenst Mk-III" if adopted. But its anachronistic design concept (naturally) kept it from adoption, and it came to be called by its unflattering development codename, "Alteisen" (German for "old iron").

A large space battleship of the <United Colony Corps> and Federation Army. A command ship often used as fleet flagship, it has excellent search and craft control systems. It is made up of a carrier for fighters and <Armored Module> units plus five beam gunships, which can act alone or be evacuated and used as missiles.
A spider-type unmanned weapon of the alien race called the "Aerogators," mainly for ground combat and base defense. Earth ID code: "AGX-02 Spider."
A spider-type unmanned weapon of the alien "Aerogators." An improved Yirmeyah.

A large Aerogator mobile weapon that also acts as a fast battlefield control unit. Using its Calcaria Pulse Tirgem (TK detector-amplifier), it excels at all-range attacks with countless small remote turrets launched from its body. Earth ID code: "AGX-06 Gryphon."

A large unmanned Aerogator mobile weapon. With its command functions removed, it is in effect a mass-production Weikel, usually remote-controlled by an outside Calcaria Pulse Tirgem (TK detector-amplifier) user.

A Personal Trooper from the <ATX Project>. Around the start of the DC War, Dr. Marion Radom heavily modified prototype unit 3 (PTX-007-03 "Gespenst Mk-II Type-T") to improve the RPT-007 "MP Gespenst Mk-II," then entering mass production as a main unit. The Mk-II was a fine ground weapon but had weak anti-air ability under gravity and short flight time, so Weissritter was first meant to get a large vernier thruster unit and main wings on its back. But a sudden decision to adopt Armored Module (Lion series) tech leaked from the EOTI Institute (later the DC) and a compact <Tesla Drive> gave it a sleeker way to fly alone under gravity. Small verniers across the body for high-speed space combat, working with the Tesla Drive, also boosted its mobility. With a plasma generator replacing its fusion generator, a customized <TC-OS>, and pilot Excellen Browning, its overall performance surpassed the Lion series. Its main weapon, the Oxtongue Launcher, switches between solid rounds and beams for superb ranged combat. But chasing mobility left its armor fragile, and with high production costs, mass production was shelved. In battle it often fights alongside Alteisen and excels at coordinated attacks with it.

The second Valsion series unit, built by <DC> leader Bian Zoldark for his daughter Lüne. Artificial muscles transmit power throughout its body, giving it far more flexible, human movement than any Personal Trooper or Armored Module (even its facial expression changes). It also has an improved compact <Tesla Drive> for solo flight. Armed with the wide-area Psychoblaster plus the Valsion's Cross Smasher and Divine Arm, it has very high combat ability. Its controls incorporate the DML (Direct Motion Link) system, letting pilot and machine move as one.

A giant robot built by <DC> leader Dr. Bian Zoldark. Called the "Ultimate Robot," it is the DC's flagship. It uses cutting-edge technology based on <Meteor 3>'s <EOT>, but unlike the Granzon, it contains no actual EOT. Its powerful weapons, like the Cross Smasher and Mega Graviton Wave, let it turn the tide of battle alone. It also has a <Tesla Drive> for solo flight in the atmosphere, and a <Distortion Field> generator. Its shape may be meant to unnerve intelligent foes, or may just reflect Bian's taste; no one knows.
Mass-production model of the "Ultimate Robot" Valsion, with nearly equal performance. Seven pre-production units exist, some fitted with the <Game System>.
The Grungust's flight mode.
Grungust Unit 2's flight mode.

An Aerogator humanoid mobile weapon. A Zechariah upgrade with high mobility and versatility, also used as a command unit. Its powerful Olga Cannon outguns the Habakkuk. Earth designation: "AGX-12 Knight."

An Aerogator humanoid mobile weapon. A Zechariah upgrade with high mobility and versatility, also used as a command unit. Its powerful Olga Cannon outguns the Habakkuk. Adom's unit is an upgraded type with added attitude-control vernier thrusters and improved defense.

An Aerogator humanoid mobile weapon. A Zechariah upgrade with high mobility and versatility, also used as a command unit. Its powerful Olga Cannon outguns the Habakkuk. Sagol's unit is an upgraded type with added attitude-control vernier thrusters and a Calcalia Pulse Tilgem (a Telekinesis detector and amplifier).

An Aerogator humanoid mobile weapon. A Zechariah upgrade with high mobility and versatility, also used as a command unit. Its powerful Olga Cannon outguns the Habakkuk. Lavan's unit is an upgraded type with added attitude-control vernier thrusters and improved durability.

A mass-produced <Armored Module> used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps>. Built to fight humanoid weapons, it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade. A cheaper variant omits some features, such as command and control.

A mass-produced <Armored Module> used by the DC Guard. Built to fight humanoid weapons, it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. This is Tenzan Nakajima's unit, with a different head design. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. This is Tempest Hawker's unit, with a different head design. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. This is Thomas Pratt's unit, with a different head design. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

A Guarlion Custom (an upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>) further enhanced as Elzam V. Branstein's personal unit. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.
Grungust's heavy tank mode.
Grungust Unit 2's heavy tank mode.

An unmanned weapon believed used by aliens other than the Aerogators. Its advanced sensors suit it to recon, including recon in force, and patrol. Earth codename: "Urchin." It lacks the "AGX" code marking Aerogator weapons.

The <DC>'s key asset: an attack nuclear submarine carrier. It carries <Armored Module> units and fires ballistic and cruise missiles. Bigger than older subs, yet stealthier and more agile. With these carriers and Armored Modules outclassing fighters, the DC's blitzkrieg ran rings around the Earth Federation Army.

An anti-alien Armored Module developed by the <EOTI Institute>. It runs on an annihilation engine Shu built from the Aerogator <EOT> sealed in <Meteor 3>. A Kabbalah Program he secretly hid in its drive code lets it use astral energy, and Shu can control it remotely with his psychic waves. It is said to use EOT from other aliens as well, but details are unknown. Its armor is super-resistant titanium reinforced at the subatomic level. Built for firepower, armor and defense over mobility; co-designer Eric Wang said, "With a superhuman pilot, the Granzon could wipe out the world's military in a day." Though classed as an Armored Module, it is unrelated to the Lion series.

Developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute> from Grungust Type 0 and PTX-007-02 Gespenst Mk-II (Type S) data, this is a <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon>. To perform in many environments, it transforms into a flight mode (Wing Gust) and heavy tank mode (Gust Lander). Its VG Alloy (Variable Geometric Alloys) armor, an active metal, lets it transform largely free of structural and shape limits. Powered by a plasma reactor, its joints use TGC Joints that control inertial mass via gravity control to reduce stress. Built-in weapons like the Boost Knuckle and Final Beam make it strong in close combat. A brainwave control unit and voice-input weapon selector assist the pilot. The best-balanced of the demanding Grungust series, it is nicknamed the "Super Fighter." Two more units exist.

Developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute> from Grungust Type 0 and PTX-007-02 Gespenst Mk-II (Type S) data, this is a <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon>. This is Unit 2 (SRG-01-2), fitted with a lion-type head. To perform in many environments, it transforms into a flight mode (Wing Gust) and heavy tank mode (Gust Lander). Its VG Alloy (Variable Geometric Alloys) armor, an active metal, lets it transform largely free of structural and shape limits. Powered by a plasma reactor, its joints use TGC Joints that control inertial mass via gravity control to reduce stress. Built-in weapons like the Boost Knuckle and Final Beam make it strong in close combat. Its base specs match Unit 1, but it carries the <T-LINK> System as a control aid.

An anti-alien <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon> from the <SRX Project> of the Earth Federation Army's Far East Branch (later Far East Command). Successor to the Grungust (Type 1), it is a mass-production prototype with some transformation and weapons omitted. Less powerful than the original, it is easier to handle than other Grungusts. Its low mobility and tough handling remain, so Unit 1 carries a special <T-LINK System>. Like the Type 1, it uses a plasma reactor, VG Alloy and TGC Joints. Two more units exist.

A <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon> built by the <Tesla Reich Institute> for the Earth Sphere Defense Committee to fight aliens. Its concept is physical attack by sheer mass; its size and shape were chosen for psychological effect, such as intimidation, on intelligent foes. Built to fight enemies too powerful for Personal Troopers, it has tremendous output and attack power. It runs on a fusion generator made for spacecraft, and its dedicated weapon, the giant Type-0 Zankanto, can cut battleship-sized objects in two, as its name says. High-thrust Boosters and trim balancers on its back allow free-flowing swordplay with the Zankanto, and TGC Joints use gravity control to manage inertial mass and reduce load.

An aerial carrier used by the <DC>. It can launch and land fighters and <Armored Modules> midair and carries many. Strong air defense and fixed arms make it a flying fortress. As the ship of DC leader Bian Zoldark and vice leader Ardler Koch, it is the DC's sub-flagship.
Albatross-class battleship flagship of Operation SRW's space fleet, carrying commander Norman Slay.

The third Space Noah-class battle carrier, built to fight aliens. It floats on a <Tesla Drive> and is driven by eight main rocket engines. Its bow module is a rock-crushing Giant Rotating Ram (the Excalibur Drill anti-ship/anti-rock ram), for melee against ships and clearing obstacles like rock or ice. Above a set Tesla Drive output, a T-Dot Array field, the Break Field, covers the ship; with the ram, it can break through wide-area <Energy Fields> like those of enemy fortresses. Codename: Iron 3.

The first Personal Trooper, developed by <Mao Industries>. Its manipulators make weapon swaps easy, and walking and hovering let it cross rough terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot only judges the situation and gives minimal input; the unit picks the right motions itself to do what the pilot intends. In the atmosphere, though, it cannot fly alone and is limited to jumps and brief glides. After rollout it was coded Type R (Rapidity) and modified to extend airtime after jumps and improve mobility and maneuverability. It was reportedly upgraded further during the DC War and deployed in combat during the L5 Campaign.

A Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries>. Its manipulators make weapon swaps easy, and walking and hovering let it cross rough terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot only judges the situation and gives minimal input; the unit picks the right motions itself to do what the pilot intends. In the atmosphere, though, it cannot fly alone and is limited to jumps and brief glides. After rollout it was coded Type S (Strength) and slated for upgrades adding powerful built-in weapons and heavier armor. However, it went missing in space along with its pilot, Colonel Kar-wai Lau, leader of the Tactical Instructor Corps.

The Gespenst Mk-II is the successor to the PTX-001 Gespenst, a mass-production prototype. Three units were built: Unit 1, Type R (Rapidity); Unit 2, Type S (Strength); and Unit 3, Type T (Test). Of these, Type R emphasizes mobility and maneuverability. Its back verniers and thrusters are also stronger, extending airtime after jumps under gravity beyond the Gespenst's. After the <DC War> broke out, its power source was replaced with a plasma generator, with upgrades throughout, and it was deployed as Major Gilliam Jaeger's unit.

The Gespenst Mk-II is the successor to the PTX-001 Gespenst, a mass-production prototype. Three units were built: Unit 1, Type R (Rapidity); Unit 2, Type S (Strength); and Unit 3, Type T (Test). Of these, Type S emphasizes built-in firepower, melee ability and defense. Its back verniers and thrusters are also stronger, extending airtime after jumps under gravity beyond the Gespenst's.

The mass-production version of the Gespenst Mk-II, a <Personal Trooper> developed by <Mao Industries>. Its manipulators make weapon swaps easy, and walking and hovering let it cross rough terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot only judges the situation and gives minimal input; the unit picks the right motions itself to do what the pilot intends. In the atmosphere, though, it cannot fly alone and is limited to jumps and brief glides. Type TT is a variant of the MP Gespenst Mk-II carrying a prototype <T-LINK System>, which also serves as an auxiliary control system to simplify the interface.

A variant of the Lion, a mass-production <Armored Module> used by the <United Colony Corps>. Official name: Lion Type C; Cosmolion is a nickname. Specialized for space, its large Booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> boosts top speed and range. Missile containers are mounted on its back. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can even operate under gravity.

A variant of the Lion, a mass-production <Armored Module> used by the <United Colony Corps>. Official name: Lion Type CF; Cosmolion is a nickname. Type F denotes enhanced weapons. Specialized for space, its large Booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> boosts top speed and range. Missile containers are mounted on its back. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can even operate under gravity.

A variant of the Lion, a mass-production <Armored Module> used by the <United Colony Corps>. Official name: Lion Type CV; Cosmolion is a nickname. Specialized for space, its large Booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> boosts top speed and range (Type V is enhanced further in this respect). Missile containers are mounted on its back. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can even operate under gravity.
Cybuster's cruising form, modeled on the divine bird Dishnas of Holy Langran. Its transform call: "Cybuster Change, Cybird!"

Built in the Holy Kingdom of Langran in the underworld La Gias. Blessed by the wind spirit Cyfis, it is called the Masou Kishin of Wind. Its main power is a Fulcanelli perpetual motion engine, boosted by the prana of its operator (pilot). Prana, essentially "ki" or "aura," comes from the operator, so its power depends heavily on the operator's aptitude. Highly airtight, it can act underwater or in space, and an internal recycling system sustains the operator for long periods. It uses ether (massless energy at rest relative to absolute coordinates) as a magical medium for propulsion. Its Orichalconium armor has talismanic numerological patterns sealed in at the particle level, giving strong magical defense. Its Laplace Demon main computer calculates causality to predict events, though this depends greatly on the operator's magic power. "Cybuster" is not its true name but a guardian name against magical attacks.

A variant of the Armored Module Lion. Official name: Lion Type S; Sealion is a nickname. Specialized for underwater combat, it has a stealthy electric propulsion system. With a Tesla Drive and rocket boosters, it can also fly for short periods.

A <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon> for fighting aliens and defending warships. It began as a giant base-defense weapon built by the Earth Federation Army in S.C. 171 to suppress the NID4 colony independence movement. Later assigned as escort to the deep-space explorer Hiryu, it went beyond Pluto's orbit but was wrecked by Aerogator mobile weapons. Back at Icarus Base, it was refitted with four limbs and reborn as a large humanoid weapon. Since its base predates PT and special humanoid weapon tech, its overall performance and stability are low, but its melee and defense are high.

A prototype built by <Mao Industries> after the Gespenst. To fix flaws found in Earth Federation Army trials of the Gespenst--armor a little thinner than planned and poor long-range accuracy with handheld weapons--it got heavier armor and Twin Beam Cannons fixed on both shoulders. It proved capable as a support and artillery unit, but high production cost and long maintenance were problems.

A prototype built by <Mao Industries> after the Gespenst. To fix flaws found in Earth Federation Army trials of the Gespenst--armor a little thinner than planned and poor long-range accuracy with handheld weapons--it got heavier armor and Twin Beam Cannons fixed on both shoulders. It proved capable as a support and artillery unit, but high production cost and long maintenance were problems. So it was never mass-produced, but was sent to the SRX Team to gather data for new models, becoming Raidiese F. Branstein's unit. Two more of the type exist.

A large mobile weapon piloted by Aerogator leader Levi Torah. As the core of the automated planet Nebiim, it is rarely used in battle. Its self-aware, autonomous metal cells, Zfylud Crystal, let it self-repair. Its Calcaria Pulse Tilgem (a Telekinesis sensor/amplifier) turns Levi's vast psychic power to attack and defense, and it can transform to suit its attacks. Earth code: AGX-14 White Deathcross.

First of the Space Noah-class battle carriers, built to fight aliens. It floats on a <Tesla Drive> and is driven by eight main rocket engines. Its super-resistant metal hull lets it fly in space and atmosphere and dive underwater. It excels at ship bombardment and carrying PTs and fighters. Its swappable bow module is a hangar and extra catapult, giving it the class's largest capacity. Codename: Platinum 1.
A <DC> aerial combat carrier. Fighters and Armored Modules can launch and land midair; capacity is high. Strong area air defense and heavy fixed arms make it a flying fortress.

An Aerogator humanoid weapon. Built for space combat but able to fight on land, it has high defense and excels up close. It's sent in against hostile civilizations Megillot can't handle. Earth code: "AGX-07 Soldier."

The Aerogators' ultimate weapon. It's <Meteor 3>, which fell on <Aidoneus Island>, transformed by the self-aware, autonomous metal cells sealed within it, the "Zfylud Crystal." It's programmed to activate when Judecca is destroyed or judged likely to be. It then shows unexpected power, wiping out threats or forcibly absorbing them via the Zfylud Crystal. The Aerogators' first and last trump card on Earth, it wasn't used at first, since activating it would end any chance of spurring humanity's own "evolution as weapons." Earth code: "AGX-15 Meteor 3."

A large transport used by the <Earth Federation Army> and <United Colony Corps> that flies both in and out of the atmosphere. Its variable payload module takes any cargo, carrying not only 20 m-class humanoid weapons but <Super Robots> as well. A launch catapult lets units sortie mid-flight for rapid deployment.
