Shura General Magnus the Heavy Quake's Chou-class Shura God. Its bloated body, huge arms and thick shell look almost comical, but saying so earns Magnus's wrath. It mostly fights by brute force, crushing foes with its sheer weight. Lacking anything like legs, it moves with thrusters in its arms.

A special humanoid weapon for sword combat. Its "Direct Feedback System" relays the pilot's thoughts straight to the machine, and it wields slashing weapons like the "Godaiken." Its cape is a shield that can even deflect beams. Likely developed alongside the Soulgain, it shares many parts, but lacks the "Direct Action Link System" that lets man and machine move as one. Its tracking and response trail the Soulgain's, but stronger thrusters give it a higher top speed.

The second Valsion series unit, built by <DC> leader Bian Zoldark for his daughter Lüne. Artificial muscles transmit power throughout its body, giving it far more flexible, human movement than any Personal Trooper or Armored Module (even its facial expression changes). It also has an improved compact <Tesla Drive> for solo flight. Armed with the wide-area Psychoblaster plus the Valsion's Cross Smasher and Divine Arm, it has very high combat ability. Its controls incorporate the DML (Direct Motion Link) system, letting pilot and machine move as one.

A space combat version of the mass-produced Valsion (Valsion Custom). The flexible arms of the pre-production model were replaced with booster units, and its armor was strengthened. Additional attitude control verniers and thrusters make it specialized for space combat, though it can also fight under gravity.
The Grungust's flight mode.
Grungust Unit 2's flight mode.
The Excellence with its space-combat "Cosmo Driver" frame. A large back booster raises agility and mobility over other frames, and long-range Fairy guided weapons allow all-range attacks.

The Excellence's first frame; this general-purpose humanoid weapon adapts to any battlefield by swapping frames. The ground-combat Striker has a detachable Arm Weapon System on its right hand, and uses its high speed for close attacks like the Crusher Arm.

The Excellence fitted with the aerial-combat "Flyer" frame. Movable boosters on its back wings allow flexible evasion, and it attacks with the Destruction Rifle. Linking the Destruction Rifle to the unit's generator also enables MAX Mode.

Shura King Alkaid's Ten-class Shura God. The Ten-class, above the Gou and Chou classes, is the mightiest of the <Shura Gods>; only two exist, Extim included. It resembles an iron giant riding a huge supreme dragon (a beast of Shura realm legend) and has fearsome power. Pickier about its pilot than any Gou- or Chou-class, Extim found no one for centuries and stayed sealed in the old Shura Castle, until Alkaid recently broke the seal and became its pilot.
War doll of the girl Despinis, servant of a mystery being called "Him." Three-faced, it excels at long range. Its fierce attacks belie its sad, pitying faces and daze foes.

A mass-production AM used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>. Isurugi Heavy Industries kept building it postwar for DC remnants and the Earth Federation Army (Federation model RAM-006). Built to fight humanoid mobile weapons, it's a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's AM, it acts as a fast theater control unit keeping pace with Lion main formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, a high-efficiency thruster separating gravitational and inertial mass, shapes its T-Dot Array into a repulsion and inertia control field that shields it. It also fixes the scant weapons of its two predecessors (Lion, Barrelion); with the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, melee blades included. Cheaper versions omitting command functions and more also exist.

An upgraded mass-production <Armored Module> Guarlion with better maneuverability. Built to fight humanoid mobile weapons, it's a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's AM, it acts as a fast theater control unit keeping pace with Lion main formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, a high-efficiency thruster separating gravitational and inertial mass, forms its T-Dot Array into a repulsion and inertia control field that shields it. It also fixes the scant weapons of its two predecessors (Lion, Barrelion); with the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, melee blades included.

The mercenary Murata's unit. Based on the Guarlion Custom, it adds large shoulder boosters for more burst speed and charge power. With reinforced armor and a Shishioh Blade, it's built for sword combat.
Grungust's heavy tank mode.
Grungust Unit 2's heavy tank mode.

Like the Astelion, a Series 77 unit developed by <Project TD>. This is Unit 1, flown by Slay Presty. A prototype of the Series 77's final model "Beta," it's codenamed "Beta Proto." Though a testbed for a new <Tesla Drive>, it's armed at the request of <Isurugi Heavy Industries>, Project TD's de facto sponsor. With mobility and maneuverability far beyond current <Armored Module> designs, it can be formidable in skilled hands.

An unmanned weapon believed used by aliens other than the Aerogators. Its advanced sensors suit it to recon, including recon in force, and patrol. Earth codename: "Urchin." It lacks the "AGX" code marking Aerogator weapons.
An upgraded Garoika, the Inspectors' unmanned mobile weapon. Its advanced sensors suit it to recon (in force) and patrols. It uses Earth-made ammo, so resupply is easy.
The Inspectors' small unmanned multi-legged turret. Earth-made missiles and ammo ease resupply.

Shura strategist Mizar the Fierce Quake's Chou-class Shura God. Odd even among <Shura Gods>, it resembles a dinosaur with drills for feet. Mizar, who handles Shura tech like analyzing the Tenku Demon Castle, rebuilt it himself. After many styles, he settled on drills, and it was specialized for them.

An anti-alien Armored Module developed by the <EOTI Institute>. It runs on an annihilation engine Shu built from the Aerogator <EOT> sealed in <Meteor 3>. A Kabbalah Program he secretly hid in its drive code lets it use astral energy, and Shu can control it remotely with his psychic waves. It is said to use EOT from other aliens as well, but details are unknown. Its armor is super-resistant titanium reinforced at the subatomic level. Built for firepower, armor and defense over mobility; co-designer Eric Wang said, "With a superhuman pilot, the Granzon could wipe out the world's military in a day." Though classed as an Armored Module, it is unrelated to the Lion series.

One of the Retsu-class <Shura Gods> flown by the Shura. Retsu-class units are dead copies of surviving Gou-class ones: weaker, but mass-producible. Gremor resembles an armadillo, using armor plates spread to each side for offense and defense. Flown mainly by Shura with speed and technique, it fights at any range.

Developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute> from Grungust Type 0 and PTX-007-02 Gespenst Mk-II (Type S) data, this is a <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon>. To perform in many environments, it transforms into a flight mode (Wing Gust) and heavy tank mode (Gust Lander). Its VG Alloy (Variable Geometric Alloys) armor, an active metal, lets it transform largely free of structural and shape limits. Powered by a plasma reactor, its joints use TGC Joints that control inertial mass via gravity control to reduce stress. Built-in weapons like the Boost Knuckle and Final Beam make it strong in close combat. A brainwave control unit and voice-input weapon selector assist the pilot. The best-balanced of the demanding Grungust series, it is nicknamed the "Super Fighter." Two more units exist.

Developed at the <Tesla Reich Institute> from Grungust Type 0 and PTX-007-02 Gespenst Mk-II (Type S) data, this is a <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon>. This is Unit 2 (SRG-01-2), fitted with a lion-type head. To perform in many environments, it transforms into a flight mode (Wing Gust) and heavy tank mode (Gust Lander). Its VG Alloy (Variable Geometric Alloys) armor, an active metal, lets it transform largely free of structural and shape limits. Powered by a plasma reactor, its joints use TGC Joints that control inertial mass via gravity control to reduce stress. Built-in weapons like the Boost Knuckle and Final Beam make it strong in close combat. Its base specs match Unit 1, but it carries the <T-LINK> System as a control aid.

Unit 3 (SRG-03-3) of the newest Grungust, built by the <Tesla Reich Institute> for the SRX Project, unfrozen after the L5 Campaign. Based on the Grungust (Type-1), it's further tuned for close combat, with the series' top output and power. It separates into the G-Raptor, a large fighter (upper body), and the G-Bison, a heavy tank (lower body), each with one pilot. After the <Inspector Incident>, Unit 3 was refit, gaining a T-LINK System and Tesla Drive plus the Type-3 Shishioh Blade (a large Super Robot Shishioh Blade).

An anti-alien <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon> from the <SRX Project> of the Earth Federation Army's Far East Branch (later Far East Command). Successor to the Grungust (Type 1), it is a mass-production prototype with some transformation and weapons omitted. Less powerful than the original, it is easier to handle than other Grungusts. Its low mobility and tough handling remain, so Unit 1 carries a special <T-LINK System>. Like the Type 1, it uses a plasma reactor, VG Alloy and TGC Joints. Two more units exist.

An anti-alien <Special Humanoid Mobile Weapon> built by the <Tesla Reich Institute> for the Earth Sphere Defense Committee. Centered on physical attacks using sheer mass, its size and shape are designed to intimidate intelligent foes. Made to fight foes too strong for Personal Troopers, it has exceptional output and power. Its own colossal Type-0 Zankanto ("ship-slaying sword") can, true to its name, cleave battleship-class objects in two. Back-mounted high-thrust boosters and sword trim balancers allow free-flowing Zankanto swordplay. TGC Joints use gravity control to manage inertial mass and cut joint stress. Refit after the Inspector Incident, it now runs on a Plasma Reactor.

The third Space Noah-class battle carrier, built to fight aliens. It floats on a <Tesla Drive> and is driven by eight main rocket engines. Its bow module is a rock-crushing Giant Rotating Ram (the Excalibur Drill anti-ship/anti-rock ram), for melee against ships and clearing obstacles like rock or ice. Above a set Tesla Drive output, a T-Dot Array field, the Break Field, covers the ship; with the ram, it can break through wide-area <Energy Fields> like those of enemy fortresses. Codename: Iron 3.

A Personal Trooper created by heavily upgrading the PTX-001 Gespenst. It's the first unit born from the "Halloween Plan," a Gespenst series upgrade proposal by Gilliam Jaeger, Kai Kitamura and others. Using <Mao Industries>' latest tech, it was rebuilt from the frame up, with nearly all armor replaced. A large flight unit with a <Tesla Drive> on its back gives it maneuverability rivaling the newest units. It also wields the Mega Buster Cannon, a powerful beam weapon.

The Gespenst Mk-II is the successor to the PTX-001 Gespenst, a mass-production prototype. Three units were built: Unit 1, Type R (Rapidity); Unit 2, Type S (Strength); and Unit 3, Type T (Test). Of these, Type R emphasizes mobility and maneuverability. Its back verniers and thrusters are also stronger, extending airtime after jumps under gravity beyond the Gespenst's. After the <DC War> broke out, its power source was replaced with a plasma generator, with upgrades throughout, and it was deployed as Major Gilliam Jaeger's unit.

The Gespenst Mk-II is the successor to the PTX-001 Gespenst, a mass-production prototype. Three units were built: Unit 1, Type R (Rapidity); Unit 2, Type S (Strength); and Unit 3, Type T (Test). Of these, Type S emphasizes built-in firepower, melee ability and defense. Its back verniers and thrusters are also stronger, extending airtime after jumps under gravity beyond the Gespenst's.

A mass-production <Armored Module> Lion variant used by DC remnants. Its official name is "Lion Type C"; "Cosmolion" is a nickname. Specialized for space combat, it has a large booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> for greater top speed and range. It also has a back-mounted missile container. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can operate under gravity.

A mass-production <Armored Module> Lion variant used by DC remnants. Its official name is "Lion Type CF"; "Cosmolion" is a nickname. The F means enhanced weaponry. Specialized for space combat, it has a large booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> for greater top speed and range. It also has a back-mounted missile container. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can operate under gravity.

A mass-production <Armored Module> Lion variant used by DC remnants. Its official name is "Lion Type CV"; "Cosmolion" is a nickname. Specialized for space combat, it has a large booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> for greater top speed and range (Type V improves these further). It also has a back-mounted missile container. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can operate under gravity.

A super robot piloted by Kota Azuma, a.k.a. Fighter Roar. Also called "Battle Force Robo" and "Compati Kaiser." Asakusa inventor Kisaburo Azuma built it from parts of a wrecked mystery robot. It runs on the "OG (Over Gate) Engine," but the engine isn't fully repaired, so the Compatible Kaiser can't show its true power yet. Main weapons include the Spiral Knuckle and Kaiser Burst.
Cybuster's cruising form, modeled on the divine bird Dishnas of Holy Langran. Its transform call: "Cybuster Change, Cybird!"

Built in the Holy Kingdom of Langran in the underworld La Gias. Blessed by the wind spirit Cyfis, it is called the Masou Kishin of Wind. Its main power is a Fulcanelli perpetual motion engine, boosted by the prana of its operator (pilot). Prana, essentially "ki" or "aura," comes from the operator, so its power depends heavily on the operator's aptitude. Highly airtight, it can act underwater or in space, and an internal recycling system sustains the operator for long periods. It uses ether (massless energy at rest relative to absolute coordinates) as a magical medium for propulsion. Its Orichalconium armor has talismanic numerological patterns sealed in at the particle level, giving strong magical defense. Its Laplace Demon main computer calculates causality to predict events, though this depends greatly on the operator's magic power. "Cybuster" is not its true name but a guardian name against magical attacks.

A variant of the Armored Module Lion. Official name: Lion Type S; Sealion is a nickname. Specialized for underwater combat, it has a stealthy electric propulsion system. With a Tesla Drive and rocket boosters, it can also fly for short periods.

An upgraded Giganscudo. Its joints use the TGC Joints of the Grungust series, and its Siege Shield Units became Siege Anchor Units, boosting melee ability. An improved Gravicon System lets it deploy a G-Territory, further raising its defense. The Duro (Italian for "hard") conversion was planned by Dr. Marion Radom. It is nicknamed "Gandoro."

One of the Retsu-class <Shura Gods> flown by the Shura. Retsu-class units are dead copies of surviving Gou-class ones: weaker, but mass-producible. Sitri resembles a cat and is flown by female Shura. It fights with agile moves, sharp claws and a nimble tail, rivaling any other Shura God. Its throat is a weak spot; the right stimulation there sharply saps its fighting power.

A prototype built by <Mao Industries> after the Gespenst. To fix flaws found in Earth Federation Army trials of the Gespenst--armor a little thinner than planned and poor long-range accuracy with handheld weapons--it got heavier armor and Twin Beam Cannons fixed on both shoulders. It proved capable as a support and artillery unit, but high production cost and long maintenance were problems.

Built on Dr. Marion Radom's plan, this is Leona Garstein's Guarlion Custom, upgraded with love by her boyfriend Tasuku Shinguji. With the latest Personal Trooper tech and a <Tesla Drive>, its mobility and firepower are improved; it also has a <T-LINK System>. Like the Guarlion, extra field inductors on its shoulders let it fix induction-heated metal particles ahead of the unit, wrap them in a TK Field and extend them to strike.

A humanoid mobile weapon that fights using only its fists and elbows. A Direct Feedback System relaying the pilot's thoughts and a Direct Action Link System mirroring the pilot's moves give it high responsiveness and agility. Artificial muscles power its body, making it supple and unrivaled in melee. The Federation calls it "Mustache Man" after its head shape.

A carrier-based attacker of the Neue DC. Small, light, cheap and easy to maintain, it usually flies from Rhinoceros-class land carriers and Trilobite-class carriers. Its short takeoff run suits fast scrambles.

A dark emperor opening dimensional doors to rule worlds; Roa's nemesis. It has the all-seeing Anpagan eye and the Kaimei Brain, an advanced spirit computer. It holds the minds of many beings it absorbed, but details are unknown. Wrecked by Roa and the Compatible Kaiser, it was healing and biding its time.
Dark Brain's second attack form. Its true self is the Kaimei Brain, which is said to change form and name over time.

The first of the Dynamic General Guardian series, designed by <DC> leader Bian Zoldark, and also called the "Double G" from its initials. A <Super Robot>-type humanoid built for sword and melee combat, it was originally made to defend the Earth Cradle, an underground cryosleep facility. Bian is said to have designed it from the start for Sänger alone, and no one else can pilot it. Its DML (Direct Motion Link) system lets man and machine move as one. Special artificial muscles drive its body, making it far more supple and dynamic than other humanoids its size.
The war puppet of Tis, a girl serving a mystery being called "That One." Small and frail-looking, it summons the big war puppet "Pater" for strong combo attacks.
Duminas's final form. With Duminas Proton as its core, it is a large war doll combining the traits of Teugatel, Hypo-Krisis and Eleos.
A being from another world. Possibly a bio-computer made by someone, but details are unknown.

The second Space Noah-class multipurpose combat carrier, built to fight aliens. It floats on a <Tesla Drive> and is driven by eight main rocket engines. Its super-resistant metal hull lets it cruise space, fly in atmosphere and dive underwater. With strong anti-ship guns and room for Personal Troopers and fighters, it realized the Federation's "ISA" tactic (Integrated Synchronizing Attack: a blitz by a carrier-battleship and its humanoid weapons). The class's purpose split into opposites, "escort for an Earth exodus fleet" and "<PT> carrier for fighting aliens," and, undercutting the main exodus plan, it was given the combat power the Earth Sphere defense plan required. To hide this, it used a flexibility unheard of in warships: a modular design with hull and main engines as a common core, letting mission-specific combat modules be replaced fairly quickly. The bow is the replaced part; ships one, two and three each carry a different module. The Hagane's bow holds the Tronium Buster Cannon, a high-output heavy metal particle cannon, giving it top-class firepower among Federation warships. Code name: "Steel 2."

A humanoid mobile weapon of the category called <Gestalt>, developed by <Wong> Heavy Industries. Its multi-jointed frame improves its ability to react on its own, and its concept is unprecedented survivability and versatility drawn from a near-human form. It is based on the prototype Gestalt VTX-000 Mironga, though its shape differs from that unit. A high-performance <Tesla Drive> on its back gives it outstanding mobility and agility. Movable pylons on its shoulders let it mount a wide range of equipment, including missiles, heavy weapons, multi-dischargers and melee weapons. The waist cockpit comes in several variants: one carries a pilot like the Mironga, one houses an ODE System bio-core, and one holds an unmanned control unit. Its head also serves as an ODE System terminal, networking with other units to share all kinds of data. It excels at high-speed coordinated combat, but because the frame was lightened for mobility, its armor is fragile.

A humanoid mobile weapon of the category called <Gestalt>, developed by <Wong> Heavy Industries. Its multi-jointed frame improves its ability to react on its own, and its concept is unprecedented survivability and versatility drawn from a near-human form. It is based on the prototype Gestalt VTX-000 Mironga, though its shape differs from that unit. A high-performance <Tesla Drive> on its back gives it outstanding mobility and agility. Movable pylons on its shoulders let it mount a wide range of equipment, including missiles, heavy weapons, multi-dischargers and melee weapons. The waist cockpit comes in several variants: one carries a pilot like the Mironga, one houses an ODE System bio-core, and one holds an unmanned control unit. Its head also serves as an ODE System terminal, networking with other units to share all kinds of data. It excels at high-speed coordinated combat, but because the frame was lightened for mobility, its armor is fragile.

A Shura God for Shura Soldiers, who may not bear names. Bat-shaped, it can fly, but has short range and is barely faster than running. Weak in attack and flown by the lowest Shura, it harasses and scouts on superiors' orders.

A heavy <Armored Module> for long-range fire support, used by the DC and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>. Isurugi Heavy Industries still builds it for DC remnants and the Federation alike (Federation model RAM-005). It looks like a huge gun, yet moves on its own and can even fly with a <Tesla Drive>. A T-Dot Array reinforces its armor and other parts, giving a sturdy frame with minimal material. Beyond its essential modules it is simply built, so it is easy to maintain and cheap to mass-produce.

An upgraded Barrelion with stronger armor and extra attitude thrusters. It looks like a huge gun, yet moves on its own and can even fly with a <Tesla Drive>. A T-Dot Array reinforces its armor and other parts, giving a sturdy frame with minimal material. Beyond its essential modules it is simply built, so it is easy to maintain and cheap to mass-produce.

An upgraded Barrelion with stronger armor. It looks like a huge gun, yet moves on its own and can even fly with a <Tesla Drive>. A T-Dot Array reinforces its armor and other parts, giving a sturdy frame with minimal material. Beyond its essential modules it is simply built, so it is easy to maintain and cheap to mass-produce.

The first <EOT>-equipped Personal Trooper, developed by <Mao Industries> at the request of the Earth Federation Army's Far East Branch. Planned as a next-gen mainline candidate beyond the mass-produced Gespenst Mk-II, it was developed from the Wildschwein. Three were built under the model number PTX-008. Minimal built-in weapons cut weight and cost, an updated <TC-OS> improved handling and hand-weapon accuracy, and an improved plasma generator gave it more output than the Wildschwein. Midway through, it was fitted with the Black Hole Engine, an EOT found in <Meteor 3> (some say the Earth Sphere Defense Committee all but forced the <EOTI Institute> to supply it, others that the Institute offered it to Mao Industries itself), giving it far more output and firepower on paper than planned. The model numbers then changed: RTX-008L and RTX-008R for the Black Hole Engine units, and RTX-009 for the one with the planned plasma generator. However, the 008R ran out of control during an activation test, wiping out the base where it was held. This earned the Hückebein the shameful nickname "Vanishing Trooper." The surviving 008L was sealed, but is rumored to have seen combat in the L5 Campaign.

An improved, mass-production prototype of the Hückebein, the first <EOT>-equipped Personal Trooper. It lacks the Black Hole Engine behind the Hückebein's accident, and its joints and inner frame come from the Gespenst Mk-II, but it runs on a new plasma generator. Three were built, equipped with the EOT-based Gravicon System and G-Impact Cannon. Costs were cut for mass production, yet the Hückebein's basic performance was kept. Its specs impressed the Federation, which later adopted it as a mainline Personal Trooper (RPT-010 "Mass Production Hückebein Mk-II"). A compact <Tesla Drive> was considered from the start, and the design allows for it. This unit (prototype No. 1) carries the <T-LINK System>.

A Super Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries> under the <SRX Project>, which was unfrozen after the <L5 Campaign>. Based on the Hückebein Mk-II, it fully incorporates the SRX Project's know-how and <EOT>. Its development concept was "a smaller, higher-performance SRX," and its part standards are shared with the R series. Its power source is a <Tronium> Engine, the same as the SRX's. It also carries the T-LINK System and an improved Gravicon System. The Mk-III's biggest feature is the "Core Trooper System," which lets it switch between two kinds of AM parts, the "AM Gunner" for ranged combat and the "AM Boxer" for melee, but it performs excellently on its own as well. Two units were developed, Type R and Type L, and the Type R, equipped with a plasma generator, rolled out first. It was then secretly handed over to Rätsel Feinschmecker to gather various data.

A Super Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries> under the <SRX Project>, which was unfrozen after the <L5 Campaign>. Based on the Hückebein Mk-II, it fully incorporates the SRX Project's know-how and <EOT>. Its development concept was "a smaller, higher-performance SRX," and its part standards are shared with the R series. Its power source is a <Tronium> Engine, the same as the SRX's. It also carries the T-LINK System and an improved Gravicon System. The Mk-III's biggest feature is the "Core Trooper System," which lets it switch between two kinds of AM parts, the "AM Gunner" for ranged combat and the "AM Boxer" for melee, but it performs excellently on its own as well. Two units were developed, Type R and Type L, and the Type R, equipped with a plasma generator, rolled out first. It was then secretly handed over to Rätsel Feinschmecker to gather various data.

The Hückebein Mk-III fitted with the "AM Gunner," an artillery AM part. Docked, the Mk-III gains range and can fire all four G-Impact Cannons at once (Full Impact Cannon), specializing in long-range combat.

The Hückebein Mk-III fitted with the "AM Boxer," a close-combat AM part. Packed with attitude-control thrusters, it excels at high-mobility melee. The AM Boxer began as "R-SWORD," the second RW Series unit, before being reworked into an AM part for the Mk-III. Part of its transformation mechanism was kept, letting the AM Boxer turn into a sword-shaped module and ram the enemy. Though weaker than the SRX at its peak, it is easier to handle and more energy-efficient, living up to its concept of "a smaller, higher-performance SRX."
A war doll piloted by Lalia, a boy serving the mysterious "Him." Four arms, four wings; a sword-and-spear close-combat expert.

A multipurpose combat carrier converted from the Hiryu, humanity's first deep-space explorer. It was the first ship with a <Tesla Drive>. In S.C. 179, Aerogator units struck it beyond Pluto's orbit, and after heavy losses it limped back to Icarus Base in the asteroid belt. It was then rebuilt around the "ISA" tactic (Integrated Synchronizing Attack: a blitz by a carrier-battleship and its humanoid weapons) as the Hiryu Custom. Its bow mounts an <EOT>-based super-gravity shock cannon, giving it power second only to the Hagane and Kurogane. Code name: "Dragon 2."

A prototype <Personal Trooper> seeking mobility, speed, versatility and power, aimed at mainline mass production. High-thrust boosters greatly extend its post-jump airtime over the Gespenst, and its left-arm Circle Zanber boosts melee power. Powerful but hard to handle, and held back by a costly plasma generator, it never reached mass production. Still, its data and concept lived on in the Hückebein series.

A Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries> for the <ATX Project>, revived after the <L5 Campaign>. Inheriting Alteisen's concept, it is a close-combat unit normally paired with the long-range Wildfalken. It uses no <EOT>, carrying solid-ammo weapons for short- to mid-range combat, and is built on a G-II Frame instead of the H Frame of the R-1 and Hückebein series. A high-performance <Tesla Drive> on its back allows solo flight under gravity, and purging its Jacket Armor puts it into a high-mobility mode. Designed by Dr. Marion Radom; one sister unit exists.

A prototype Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries> for the <ATX Project>, revived after the <L5 Campaign>. An artillery unit inheriting Weissritter's concept, it carries a high-performance <Tesla Drive>, giving it top-class mobility among Personal Troopers. It is normally paired with the close-combat Wildwürger, and their combo with the Wildwürger in high-mobility mode, the Twin Bird Strike, is powerful. Its main weapon is the Oxtongue Rifle, which switches between solid rounds and energy shots. Unlike the Wildwürger, it uses the Hückebein-type H Frame, improving rigidity while cutting weight. Developed by Dr. Kirk Hamill. The name Wildfalken comes from the German "WILD" and "WANDERFALKE" (peregrine falcon). One sister unit exists.

Mao Industries' first transformable <Personal Trooper>. Built to fix the poor anti-air ability of the ground-based Gespenst Mk-II and Schutzwald, it can transform into a flight form (Flyer Mode) for independent atmospheric flight. Large back-mounted vernier thrusters also give it excellent hovering, jumping and airtime in PT form. Types L and R were planned, but budget and time issues halted assembly of Type R. Type L was tested with its transformation issues unresolved and was wrecked. Type R then supplied parts to Type L and was struck from the registry, and Type L went to the SRX Project for an overhaul. That data went into the R-1 then in development, making the Wildraubtier effectively its prototype.
The Wildraubtier's flight form (Flyer Mode).

Fernando's Gou-class Shura God. The Shura call it and Ialdabaoth the "twin Shura Gods"; their performance is nearly equal. Shura Gods are Shura weapons powered by the pilot's life energy, with self-repairing armor and materials. Tracing Fernando's Kishin Ken directly, it excels at close melee with one-hit-kill power. Valefor long slept with Ialdabaoth in the old Shura Castle; Fernando and Folka emerging as pilots at the same time was a stroke of luck.

Kota Azuma clad in the Roa Armor. Roa's soul dwells in the forehead crystal. Airtight, it works in space and underwater. (The hair is a heat-sink part; the nose and mouth are skin-colored armor, the eyes an ultra-thin clear shield.) Option parts mount on hardpoints all over. The armor vastly boosts Kota's physical abilities; with its small back thrusters and main weapon, the Fighter Beamgun, he can even take on humanoid mobile weapons.

An Armored Module developed by the Tesla-Leicht Institute at the request and expense of the Principality of Riksent, and Shine Hausen's personal unit. Built from a modified, downsized Astelion test frame and Tesla Drive, it is lightened to the limit, giving it mobility rivaling the Astelion. To offset its fragile armor, it carries an Energy Field generator, along with a special man-machine interface called the "W-LINK System." Type G's cockpit is custom-built for Shine, who has the power of foresight, and is fitted with a brainwave control device like the Grungust's and a high-performance G Canceller. The "W-LINK System" synchronizes the two Fairlions' movements to make up for the gap in piloting skill between Latune and Shine. Through it, Latune, piloting Type S, can partly control Type G and perform combo attacks.

An Armored Module developed by the Tesla-Leicht Institute at the request and expense of the Principality of Riksent, and Latune Subota's personal unit. Built from a modified, downsized Astelion test frame and Tesla Drive, it is lightened to the limit, giving it mobility rivaling the Astelion. To offset its fragile armor, it carries an Energy Field generator, along with a special man-machine interface called the "W-LINK System." The system synchronizes the two Fairlions' movements to make up for the gap in piloting skill between Latune and Shine. Through it, Latune, piloting Type S, can partly control Type G and perform combo attacks.

Neue DC main battle tank. Armed with a large Linear Cannon and Missile Pods, it hovers for fast movement and turning. Its canopy-like part is not a cockpit but a sensor module: optics, IR night vision, laser rangefinder.

One of the Retsu-class Shura Gods flown by the Shura. Retsu-class units are dead copies of surviving Gou-class ones: weaker, but mass-producible. Flaus resembles a bull, with great charging power. Flown mainly by Shura strong in power, it excels at charging with its horns. Its horns and mane can also be thrown, fired at foes in succession.

Shura General Masis of the Ice Spear's Chou-class Shura God. With its bluish-white body and clear wings, it is the most beautiful of the <Shura Gods>. A Chou-class forms when a Shura God with enough battle experience absorbs vast haki (life energy) from its pilot, changing form and gaining power. The Shura call this sudden evolution "Shinka," but it is risky: some pilots died, drained of haki. Its power after Shinka reflects its battle record and its pilot's nature; Peirines is said to embody Masis's sense of beauty and icy, aloof coldness. Masis's haki-turned-ice style entrances even foes, who realize too late they are frozen.

The top Barrelion model, based on the Barrelion Custom. Two Bighead Railguns raise its firepower, and its armor and mobility are further improved. It looks like a big gun, yet moves on its own and can even fly solo via a <Tesla Drive>. T-Dot Arrays reinforce its armor and more, making a sturdy frame from minimal material, so all but key modules are simple: easy to maintain and cheap enough to mass-produce.

One of the mysterious Einst. A humanoid mobile weapon made entirely of demon-like masks, piloted by Alchemie, an Einst in human form. Demon masks... said to represent "persona." What ties this unit to its pilot, Alchemie...?

A spaceship used by the Earth Federation Army and others. Its frame hull can mount weapon modules with missiles and lasers, catapult containers for <Armored Module>s and <Personal Trooper>s, or cargo containers, letting it serve as a battleship, carrier, transport, or support ship.

One of the Retsu-class Shura Gods flown by the Shura. Retsu-class units are dead copies of surviving Gou-class ones: weaker, but mass-producible. Bofry resembles a chameleon and can freely change color to match the terrain. Its attack power is low, but by bewildering foes with its tricky tongue and color changes, it occasionally defeats stronger Shura Gods.

Shura General Altis of the Flash's Chou-class Shura God. It is a centaur with a crimson body, two wings and four legs. Chou-class units are <Shura Gods> that, after enough battle, absorb vast haki (life energy) from their pilots, changing form and gaining power. The Shura call this sudden evolution "Shinka," but it is risky: some pilots died, drained of haki. Power after Shinka reflects battle record and the pilot's nature; ones with a human face, like Maldict, are rare, likely reflecting Altis's "heart" and "feelings." Maldict fights by turning Altis's haki into crimson flame, and its vivid style fills many Shura with awe.

A Gestalt-category humanoid mobile weapon developed by <Wong Heavy Industries>. Its high-performance <Tesla Drive> gives it excellent mobility. Balanced between shooting and melee, it excels at linked combat via the <AMN System>. Its frame was lightened for mobility, leaving its armor fragile.

Folka's Gou-class Shura God. Shura Gods are Shura weapons powered by the pilot's life energy, with self-repairing armor and materials. Tracing Folka's Kishin Ken directly, it excels at close melee with one-hit-kill power. Its style shines most one-on-one; in a duel it is said to rival a general's Shura God. Its wild, hair-whipping fighting has a fierce, unique air, one reason Folka is known among the Shura. With the near-identical Valefor it forms the "twin Shura Gods," especially precious among the few remaining Gou-class.

A ground artillery humanoid mobile weapon, also called Type34. A custom RGV-Type30 Randgriz using its successor's drive system and generator, with upgraded firepower and armor. With thick armor, a shield, Jammer, and Beam Coat, it's unmatched in stand-and-shoot fights.

A humanoid mobile weapon for land and artillery combat, also called Type 34. A custom Randgriz (the mass-produced RGV-Type 30) given its successor's drive system and generator for better artillery and armor. It has thick armor, a shield, a Jammer and a Beam Coat. The Razangriff Raven mounts a flight unit/armed base (with Tesla Drive and Plasma Generator) on a Razangriff. It can fly under gravity, and added arms like the Charged Particle Beam boost its firepower.

The Weissritter, transformed and powered up by unknown technology; over 60% of it has become unanalyzable. Its main weapon, the Howling Launcher, seems to be its Oxtongue Launcher transformed. It can also deploy a strong <Energy Field> and attack with thought waves.

The Extim after undergoing divinization. Its lighter frame has lowered its defense, but its speed and power have risen dramatically. Its appearance closely resembles the demon god "Mahashinou" of Shura realm legend. Perhaps because Alkaid's fighting spirit, set on the Summit of Asura, shaped the divinization, ordinary Shura lose their will to fight at the mere sight of it. Yet those Alkaid deems worthy of trading blows with can draw out power beyond their own. "Raha" is an old Shura realm word meaning "truth."

A ground artillery humanoid mobile weapon, also called Type30. Low mobility, but thick armor and high stability and reliability. It can hover over rough terrain. Cheap to build, it was mass-produced by the Neue DC for fire support.

A humanoid mobile weapon for ground and artillery combat, also called the Type 30. Its mobility is low, but its armor is thick, and the unit is highly stable and reliable. It can also hover, giving it excellent terrain handling. The Randgriz Raven is a modified Randgriz fitted with a booster pod housing a Tesla Drive. Its Linear Cannon has been doubled to two barrels, raising its firepower.

A variant of the Armored Module Lion. Its official name is "Lion Type L"; "Landlion" is a nickname. Built for ground combat, it has four stick movers instead of legs, giving it superb cross-country ability. Angling them near horizontal lowers its profile. Less mobile and agile than the Lion, it mainly attacks and defends ground bases, so it carries a large railgun stronger than the standard model's. Its <Tesla Drive> allows solo flight, but it's poor at aerial combat.

A mass-produced Armored Module used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>. Isurugi Heavy Industries kept building it after the war for DC remnants and the Earth Federation Army alike (Federation model RAM-004). Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster separating gravitational from inertial mass, cuts only gravitational mass, letting it hover on small downward jets and fly on small wings' lift. Thrust instead comes from a large conventional engine in its unusual lower body, which doubles as landing gear. Many attitude thrusters there allow bold terrain-following for ground combat, and swapping some parts lets it operate in space. Very simple for a Tesla Drive unit, it is also cheap to produce.

A mass-produced Armored Module used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>. Isurugi Heavy Industries kept building it after the war for DC remnants and the Earth Federation Army alike (Federation model RAM-004F). An improved Lion with stronger weapons. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster separating gravitational from inertial mass, cuts only gravitational mass, letting it hover on small downward jets and fly on small wings' lift. Thrust instead comes from a large conventional engine in its unusual lower body, which doubles as landing gear. Many attitude thrusters there allow bold terrain-following for ground combat, and swapping some parts lets it operate in space. Very simple for a Tesla Drive unit, it is also cheap to produce.

A mass-produced Armored Module used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>; an improved Lion with better mobility. Isurugi Heavy Industries kept building it after the <DC War>, and both DC remnants and the Earth Federation Army use it, the latter as a main unit (Federation model no. RAM-004V). Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, cuts only gravitational mass, so it floats easily on small downward jets and flies on the lift of small main wings. Thrust comes from a large conventional main engine in its unusual lower body, which doubles as landing gear. Many attitude thrusters there allow bold terrain-following, so it fights on the ground too. Swapping some parts lets it operate in space. It is very simple for a Tesla Drive unit and cheap to build.
A large strategic and tactical transport used by the Earth Federation Army. It can carry up to five Personal Troopers into battle. Its catapult lets them launch in mid-flight for rapid deployment.

A Chokijin dug up from Chiyou's Tomb in Shandong, China. RyuKoOh is two Chokijin, RyuOhKi and KoOhKi; with KoOhKi on top and RyuOhKi below, they combine into KoRyuOh. It beats RyuKoOh at ground and close combat and handles weapons well. It can't fly, but moves well on land and can create afterimages.

A Chokijin dug up from Chiyou's Tomb in Shandong, China. Said to be a semi-organic weapon the ancients made to fight demons called the Hyakuja. It thinks and acts on its own, but shows its true power only with a psychic it accepts (a Strong Psychic) aboard. Unlike its other form, KoRyuOh, it excels in air, water and long-range sorcery combat, with immense firepower.

The mass-production model of the Gespenst Mk-II, a <Personal Trooper> by <Mao Industries>. Manipulators make swapping weapons easy, and walking and hovering let it cross rough terrain. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot just judges the situation and gives minimal input; the unit picks fitting motions itself to do what the pilot intends. It can't fly unaided in the atmosphere, limited to jumps and brief glides in air combat. Performance nearly matches the pre-production Gespenst Mk-II (Type R), but its sensors are improved and its left arm has a Plasma Stake (Jet Magnum) for melee instead of a Plasma Cutter.

A large artillery mobile weapon. Its four long-range Gigante Cannone beam cannons make it a superb artillery unit. Its Tesla Drive allows solo flight under gravity. It looks like the Giganscudo before its humanoid refit, but its origins are unknown.

A mass-production Personal Trooper based on the Hückebein Mk-II. Adopted as a new main unit under the <Aegis Plan>, the Federation's arms buildup program. A standard <Tesla Drive> lets it fly alone under gravity. It lacks <EOT> and EOT-based weapons, but nearly matches the pre-production model. Its Gespenst-line G-II frame, improved from the pre-production model's, replaces the Hückebein H-frame and keeps costs low.
A Federation Army multirole fighter. 2D thrust-vectoring nozzles and large canard delta wings let it handle air combat and ground attack alike.
A space fighter used by the United Colony Corps and others. Its side units have front and rear rockets of equal thrust.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

An upgraded Guarlion, a mass-produced <Armored Module>, with enhanced mobility. The Guarlion was built to fight humanoid weapons; it is a versatile, high-performance unit whose tougher armor also suits local combat. As a commander's unit, it is a fast battlefield controller that keeps pace with Lion formations. Its <Tesla Drive>, an efficient reaction thruster that separates gravitational and inertial mass, makes the T-Dot Array a repulsion and inertia control field that shields the unit. It also fixes its predecessors' (Lion, Barrelion) lack of weapons: thanks to the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, such as a melee blade.

The <DC>'s key asset: an attack nuclear submarine carrier. It carries <Armored Module> units and fires ballistic and cruise missiles. Bigger than older subs, yet stealthier and more agile. With these carriers and Armored Modules outclassing fighters, the DC's blitzkrieg ran rings around the Earth Federation Army.

A variant of the Lion, a mass-production <Armored Module> used by the <United Colony Corps>. Official name: Lion Type CV; Cosmolion is a nickname. Specialized for space, its large Booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> boosts top speed and range (Type V is enhanced further in this respect). Missile containers are mounted on its back. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can even operate under gravity.

A variant of the Lion, a mass-production <Armored Module> used by the <United Colony Corps>. Official name: Lion Type CV; Cosmolion is a nickname. Specialized for space, its large Booster unit with an improved <Tesla Drive> boosts top speed and range (Type V is enhanced further in this respect). Missile containers are mounted on its back. With tuning and a skilled pilot, it can even operate under gravity.

The top Barrelion model, based on the Barrelion Custom. Two Bighead Railguns raise its firepower, and its armor and mobility are further improved. It looks like a big gun, yet moves on its own and can even fly solo via a <Tesla Drive>. T-Dot Arrays reinforce its armor and more, making a sturdy frame from minimal material, so all but key modules are simple: easy to maintain and cheap enough to mass-produce.

Mass-production model of the Gespenst Mk-II, a <Personal Trooper> built by <Mao Industries>. Manipulators allow easy weapon swaps, and walking and hovering give it good rough-terrain mobility. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot just assesses the situation with minimal input, and the unit automatically picks fitting motions to carry out their intent. But it can't fly alone in atmosphere, limited to jumps and short glides in the air. Performance nearly matches the pre-production Gespenst Mk-II (Type R), with better sensors and a melee Plasma Stake (Jet Magnum) on the left arm in place of the Plasma Cutter. Adopted before the DC War as the Earth Federation Army's next-gen main mobile weapon, it has suffered production delays for various reasons, so few are deployed yet.

An upgraded <Isurugi Heavy Industries> fighter. Built for any battlefield, it excels in air combat at all altitudes and carries a heavy payload. Special-material flexible wings, a buried cockpit and long-TBO modules set it apart.

An upgraded Garoika, the Inspectors' unmanned mobile weapon. Its advanced sensors suit it to recon (in force) and patrols. It uses Earth-made ammo, so resupply is easy.

A Personal Trooper developed by <Mao Industries> for the <ATX Project>, revived after the <L5 Campaign>. Inheriting Alteisen's concept, it is a close-combat unit normally paired with the long-range Wildfalken. It uses no <EOT>, carrying solid-ammo weapons for short- to mid-range combat, and is built on a G-II Frame instead of the H Frame of the R-1 and Hückebein series. A high-performance <Tesla Drive> on its back allows solo flight under gravity, and purging its Jacket Armor puts it into a high-mobility mode. Designed by Dr. Marion Radom; one sister unit exists.

A prototype <Personal Trooper> developed by <Mao Industries> under the <ATX Project>, which was unfrozen after the <L5 Campaign>. An artillery unit inheriting the Weissritter's concept, it carries a high-performance <Tesla Drive>, and its mobility ranks among the best of any Personal Trooper. Its main weapon is the Oxtongue Rifle, which switches between solid rounds and energy shots. Unlike the Wildwurger, it uses the Hückebein line's H-Frame for greater rigidity and less weight. Its lead developer is Dr. Kirk Hamill. The Type L was taken into combat by Arado Balanga during the <Inspector Incident>, but was wrecked in battle with Garghau, the <Inspectors>' commander unit.

The top Barrelion model, based on the Barrelion Custom. Two Bighead Railguns raise its firepower, and its armor and mobility are further improved. Machinery Children's humanoid mobile weapon: a Mass-Production Huckebein Mk-II altered and enhanced by Machine Cells. It has the <Game System> and remote weapons, and Machine Cells in its frame and armor grant strong self-repair.

Machinery Children's humanoid mobile weapon: a Mass-Production Huckebein Mk-II altered and enhanced by Machine Cells. It has the <Game System> and remote weapons, and Machine Cells in its frame and armor grant strong self-repair.

A large land battleship used by the DC. It boasts strong wide-area air defense and can fire ballistic and cruise missiles. It can also carry fighters and <Armored Module>s. A virtual mobile HQ and fortress, it usually stays in the rear. Its large bow ram, meant for the big ground weapons and mobile fortresses aliens (might) field, was reportedly almost never used.

The Weissritter, transformed and powered up by unknown technology; over 60% of it has become unanalyzable. Its main weapon, the Howling Launcher, seems to be its Oxtongue Launcher transformed. It can also deploy a strong <Energy Field> and attack with thought waves.

A humanoid mobile weapon for land and artillery combat, also called Type 34. A custom Randgriz (the mass-produced RGV-Type 30) given its successor's drive system and generator for better artillery and armor. It has thick armor, a shield, a Jammer and a Beam Coat. The Razangriff Raven mounts a flight unit/armed base (with Tesla Drive and Plasma Generator) on a Razangriff. It can fly under gravity, and added arms like the Charged Particle Beam boost its firepower.

The Hückebein Mk-III fitted with the "AM Gunner," an artillery AM part. Docked, the Mk-III gains range and can fire all four G-Impact Cannons at once (Full Impact Cannon), specializing in long-range combat.

The Hückebein Mk-III fitted with the "AM Boxer," a close-combat AM part. Packed with attitude-control thrusters, it excels at high-mobility melee. The AM Boxer began as "R-SWORD," the second RW Series unit, before being reworked into an AM part for the Mk-III. Part of its transformation mechanism was kept, letting the AM Boxer turn into a sword-shaped module and ram the enemy. Though weaker than the SRX at its peak, it is easier to handle and more energy-efficient, living up to its concept of "a smaller, higher-performance SRX."

A Federation Army tank. Its pivoting front tracks handle rough terrain well, but it's obsolete, replaced as MBT by the Type 82 Government.

A mass-production AM used by the <DC> and <United Colony Corps> in the <DC War>. Isurugi Heavy Industries kept building it postwar for DC remnants and the Earth Federation Army (Federation model RAM-006). It also fixes the scant weapons of its two predecessors (Lion, Barrelion); with the LIEON System's better limb control, it can wield many weapons, melee blades included. Cheaper versions omitting command functions and more also exist.

A transformed Einst Regisseur, a type of <Einst> captured by the Cry Wolves during the Inspector Incident. Mitar Zapato, head of the Tsentr Project, and his team injected it with Razumnanium, a metal cell capable of self-repair and self-evolution, turning it into something other than the Einst: the Jetzt (German for "now"). This is likely why, unlike the other <Einst>, it did not vanish with the Stern Neu Regisseur and survived.

A bioweapon spawned by the Jetzt Regisseur. It resembles the Einst Knochen, a type of <Einst>, in looks and performance, its whole body made of bone-like matter. Armed with sharp claws and blade-like parts resembling ribs, it excels at close to mid-range combat.

A bioweapon spawned by the Jetzt Regisseur. It resembles the Einst Glied, a type of <Einst>, in looks and performance, its whole body made of something like plants or blood vessels. Armed with what appears to be a long-range beam cannon, it excels at mid to long-range combat.

A semi-Super Robot mobile weapon developed by the Tsentr Project. Its high-performance built-in servomotors make it far more agile than it looks. It also carries a shield particle dispersal system that releases an electrically charged mist to disrupt enemies.

The Exellion equipped with the Eternal, a high-mobility, long-range combat frame. Designed by Mizuho Saiki for the final battle against Duminas and built at the <Tesla Reich Institute>, the Eternal Frame draws the Time Flow Engine's output to its limit, giving it firepower beyond the Striker, Flyer and Cosmo Driver. Its mobility and acceleration are also the best of all the frames.

The Exellion equipped with the Lightning, a semi-Super Robot frame. Designed by Mizuho Saiki for the final battle against Duminas and built at the <Tesla Reich Institute>, the Lightning Frame draws the Time Flow Engine's output to its limit, giving it the highest firepower of all the frames. Its armor is also reinforced, allowing close combat like a Super Robot. Compared to the Eternal Frame, a high-mobility, long-range frame developed at the same time, it is built for close-range power fighting.

A large mobile weapon sealed deep within the Swordian. It is the guardian of the Swordian's core, built with unknown technology, but details are unclear. It can teleport itself and, like the Swordian's Dagger, generate something like a transfer field to send others elsewhere.

A spatial transfer device found inside the Swordian. The Shura call it the "Shunten Blade." With three or more together, they can deploy something like a transfer field and send others to another place. Each can also teleport itself and is armed, so it can operate as a mobile weapon.
A mid-sized bioweapon spawned by the Flatfish. It is used much like a missile.
An unmanned ground weapon developed by the Tsentr Project. Originally a survey unit, it was later armed.

The Granzon powered up through alchemy and sorcery. A Kabbalah Program secretly installed by Shu Shirakawa lets it fully harness astral energy. As a result, its attack and defense far exceed those of the Granzon.

A bioweapon developed by the Tsentr Project. It went berserk after being injected with a mysterious substance called Jetzt cells. It has no mechanical parts and is closer to a monster or kaiju. It can also produce small bioweapons called Tadpoles. What looks like a tail is actually its left arm; its right arm and legs have atrophied into tentacle-like limbs. It is also called the "space flounder."
An unmanned air combat weapon developed by the Tsentr Project. Originally a reconnaissance UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle), it was later armed.
A humanoid mobile weapon piloted by Alchemie. It was a type of <Einst>, but a change in Alchemie's own nature likely let it survive rather than vanish with the Stern Neu Regisseur.

Ialdabaoth after undergoing divinization, raising it from a Roar-class to a Super-class Shura God. A divinized <Shura Gods> unit's power and abilities reflect its battle record and the nature of its pilot, and one with a human face like this Ialdabaoth is rare. This is thought to come from the heart and compassion of Folka, who seeks a new way of life for the Shura. Divinized Shura Gods usually take on a more aggressive look, but Ialdabaoth became calm, even divine in appearance. Its power is immense, surpassing other Super-class Shura Gods and said to rival even the Heaven-class, the highest rank of Shura God.
Read as "Ijin." Thought to be a type of <Chokijin>, but details are unknown. It wields a large spear-like weapon, which seems to be its true body.

A semi-Super Robot mobile weapon developed by the Tsentr Project. Its high-performance built-in servomotors make it far more agile than it looks. It also carries a shield particle dispersal system that releases an electrically charged mist to disrupt enemies.

The mass-production model of the Gespenst Mk-II, a <Personal Trooper> developed by <Mao Industries>. Its features include easy weapon swaps thanks to its manipulators and excellent terrain handling through bipedal walking and hovering. With the <TC-OS>, the pilot need only judge the situation and make minimal inputs; the unit automatically selects the right motions to carry out the pilot's intent. However, it cannot fly on its own within the atmosphere, and its air combat ability is limited to jumps and short glides. Its performance is nearly identical to the mass-production prototype Gespenst Mk-II (Type R), but its sensors are improved, and its left arm mounts a Plasma Stake (Jet Magnum) for melee combat instead of a Plasma Cutter. This unit is the personal machine of Major Albero Est, leader of the 3rd Special Operations PT Unit Cry Wolves, with an upgraded frame and weapons.
